### CORE-A-C002 — Explain public metadata and flag carriers (documentation)

`DeviceInfo`'s type and most properties have no XML describing purpose, units, defaults, provenance, or
interpretation. `ConnectionType`, `Transport`, and `Feature` similarly leave important public values or
semantics implicit. Existing guide summaries cannot substitute for usable member reference. Provide
focused contracts: supported versus enabled applications, manufacturing flags versus reported approval,
seconds for both timeouts, missing-field defaults versus observed false/zero, component versions,
effective firmware and qualifier precedence, unknown enum values, and the borrowed-buffer caveat below.
Keep `DeviceCapabilities.All` explicitly the union of currently modeled application bits, rather than a
claim to every future bit or every enabled application. Preserve open numeric values; do not turn docs
work into validation changes. `ConnectionTypeExtensions`, `PhysicalYubiKeyTests`, mapper tests, and
field-length tests provide current behavioral oracles. Reopen the public XML, Core guides, shared filters,
CLI labels, and Management reference after any decoding/default/carrier change.

### CORE-A-C003 — Returned metadata retains caller/TLV-owned bytes (implementation + documentation decision)

`DeviceInfo.CreateFromTlvs` stores `ReadFixedField(..., 0x07, 1)` directly as `ChallengeResponseTimeout`
(`DeviceInfo.cs:137,165,193`). `Tlv.Value` returns a view into its owned array; `Tlv.Dispose` clears that
array (`Utilities/Tlv.cs:65,81–88`). Therefore disposing the input TLVs changes the returned DeviceInfo's
timeout bytes. Equality and the content-based hash then depend on the input's lifetime. The public init property can likewise
receive caller-owned mutable memory. This is metadata ownership, not a secret-zeroing defect.

`DeviceInfoTests.Equals_SnapshotsDecodedFromSeparateBuffers_CompareByContent` checks before its using
declarations dispose inputs. It does not test returned-value stability after input disposal. `DeviceInfoReader`
currently leaves decoded page lists undisposed, so adding `using` mechanically would change successful
results. Decide an independently owned scalar/copy or an explicitly borrowed input lifetime in separately
scoped implementation work. Coordinate with C's TLV owner; A makes no disposition of C units.
Reopen `CreateFromTlvs`, equality remarks, `IYubiKey.CachedDeviceInfo`, Core README, discovery guide,
physical model, Management return/reference examples, and any proposed reader cleanup when ownership is
settled. Preserve the supported narrower fact that replacing a device's snapshot does not mutate the
previous struct's scalar fields. A pure managed disposal/hash vector is proposed below, unexecuted.

### CORE-A-C004 — FIPS application masks use the ordinary app decoder (inherited implementation candidate)

Aliases: `management-001:MGMT-XREF-001` and
`audit-v2-20261022-20261031:deviceinfo-FIPS-residual`, one nonadditive group.
`DeviceInfo.cs:153–154,232–239` routes 0x14/0x15 through `FromApp`; its separate `FromFips` maps
01→FIDO2, 02→PIV, 04→OpenPGP, 08→OATH, 10→HsmAuth. A one-byte 02 presently becomes U2F.
The pinned Python parser uses its FIPS-specific mapping for both fields. `CapabilityMapperTests`
tests the unused helper directly using two-byte buffers; `DeviceInfoTests` supplies ordinary application
encodings for these FIPS fields. Those oracles do not verify the actual FIPS-tag integration.
Simply switching helpers would still mishandle nonzero one-byte values because `FromFips` reads Int16.

The public vendor configuration reference has no 0x14/0x15 definition. Initial research and one focused
follow-up did not establish authoritative current tag widths/mapping. Keep this precise wire-source gap;
the Python implementation and local dead helper are strong implementation evidence, not certification
authority. Reopen Core metadata, shared FIPS filters, CLI display qualifications, and Management FIPS
tests/docs after mapping/width work and integrated nonzero vectors. Physical FIPS approval remains a
device/profile/operation question even after decoding is fixed.

### CORE-A-C005 — Flagged form factor remains an unnamed base-enum value (inherited implementation/representation decision)

Alias: `management-001:MGMT-XREF-002`. At `DeviceInfo.cs:142–146`, 0x81 produces `IsFips=true` and
`FormFactor=(FormFactor)129`, whereas the named base enum's USB-A keychain is 1. The manufacturer's
configuration table explicitly assigns 0x41/0x81 to Security Key/FIPS USB-A keychains on firmware 5.4+;
the technical manual independently lists the FIPS values. Python masks the low nibble. No current
DeviceInfo fixture verifies a nonzero product-flag byte. Shared exact enum filters can miss these keys;
labels may fall back to Unknown. Decide normalized plus preserved raw representation, then reopen
FormFactor/DeviceInfo XML, CLI formatters, shared fixture filters, Core guides, and Management examples.
Preserve unknown values deliberately instead of silently adopting Python's unknown-to-zero policy.

source_definition.text:
### CORE-A-C006 — Wide capabilities accepted but decoded from the first Int16 (inherited implementation candidate)

Alias: `audit-v2-20261022-20261031:deviceinfo-wide-app-bits`.
`ReadCapabilities` accepts nonempty variable widths; `FromApp` reads the first two bytes whenever length
exceeds one (`DeviceInfo.cs:232–239,353–359`). Thus 00 00 10 loses the trailing PIV bit; 80 00 sign-extends
through the signed Int16 into the int-backed enum. The current wide fixture contains only zeros, while
ordinary mapper vectors use at most two bytes. Python consumes the whole unsigned big-endian integer.
The vendor table establishes bit values but not an unbounded future-width promise. Decide supported
numeric width and raw preservation, and test trailing nonzero and high-bit vectors. Reopen metadata
XML, `All` wording, shared capability filters, CLI labels, and Management capability examples after that
decision. This is distinct from fixed-field guards and FIPS remapping.

### CORE-A-C007 — Interface XML still describes pre-feed events/ownership (documentation)

`IYubiKey.cs:49–52,90–97,122–124,155–158` describes a live repository/manager and metadata/serial
replacement without any device event. Current `SnapshotDiff` emits `DeviceUpdated` when retained
metadata changes, including learning a serial. `DeviceIdentityContractTests.Apply_LateSerialArrival_PopulatesRetainedObjectAndEmitsUpdate`
asserts the event. Scope retention to one owned monitor and describe updates through its change feed.
At 70–74, explain that the separate Hid group bit and All sentinel are absent, while both concrete HID
bits may be present together. A reader should not infer that FIDO+OTP cannot coexist. Reopen interface
XML and the physical-model summary after any update/serial/retention change; the newer identity guide
already describes the event and is a consistency reference, not a reason to preserve the stale XML.

source_definition.text:
### CORE-A-C008 — Read-budget/retry/internal rationale overclaims (documentation)

`DiscoveryBudgets.ScanUpperBound` is the arithmetic 5+2+3 second sum, not a scan completion bound;
identity retries, backoffs, scan-lock queueing, synchronous topology, and logging lie outside that sum.
Its XML should name the sum precisely. `DiscoveryIdentityReader` retries every ordinary exception up to
three attempts, not just classified transient PC/SC failures; cancellation propagates, skips return null,
and a timeout ends the attempt sequence. A timeout can reflect worker/PID admission or slow teardown,
so it does not prove a busy card. `SharedDeviceInfoRead` comments at 145–151 narrate old Phase-0 history;
`DiscoveryReadScope` says replacement manager; `ProtocolDeviceInfo` comments narrate an upstream change.
Describe current finder/admission/borrowed ownership and the retained release constraint instead.
The old Task.Run/SCardTransmit explanation in `DiscoveryIdentityReaderTests:62–67` predates the current
owned PC/SC lifetime. `FindYubiKeysFaultInjectionTests:252–254` says invalidation happens at event ingress;
the actual monitor does it after coalescing immediately before the scan.

`DiscoverySingleFlightTests`, `DiscoveryReadSchedulingTests`, `FindYubiKeysScopeTests`, and the actual
retry helper establish different contracts; keep their oracles distinct. Reopen local comments/XML and
the budget/monitor architecture sections when scheduling, retry classification, or cleanup changes.

source_definition.text:
### CORE-A-C009 — Topology claims need implementation and OS qualification (documentation/qualification)

`FindYubiKeys.ResolveTopologyKey` says the call never blocks meaningfully. The Windows path performs
synchronous context establishment, reader-instance queries, property resolution, and context disposal
without an SDK wait budget. Catching errors provides fallback, not a latency bound. The Windows reader
API documents the null-buffer length probe and Windows 8 minimum; it also explicitly fails under Remote
Desktop redirection with `SCARD_E_READER_UNAVAILABLE`. Container-ID documentation supports matching
devnodes in a container, not fresh hardware attestation on this host.

The null resolver and its test establish that this SDK supplies no topology keys on Linux/macOS.
Claims that no supported OS mapping exists anywhere, or that those platforms cannot group HID siblings
at all, exceed that oracle; the guarantees guide itself acknowledges HID-parent topology as unimplemented.
Qualify the current implementation and supported evidence instead. Reopen topology XML/comments, G4/G9,
platform troubleshooting, and Windows test summaries after actual native/OS evidence or implementation
changes. Preserve the Windows readiness handoff and existing hardware gap; no other branch was inspected.

### CORE-A-C010 — Merge/test explanations carry stale TODOs and stronger oracles than assertions (documentation)

`CompositeDeviceMergerVectorTests:338–347` still requests the topology vector already implemented at
414–442. Retain the completed test's real reason, rather than an unfinished Phase-3 instruction.
The same file calls DeviceId durable at 768–770, treats a complete contested census as necessarily live
at 629–632, and repeatedly narrates Phase/WAS/orchestrator decisions. The implementation expressly calls
that census a heuristic that can choose stale membership. The mixed-evidence test verifies conservation
and membership for one input order, not permutation determinism. The absent-topology test compares
specific expected shapes rather than serializing byte-identical old/new implementations. Preserve method
names/assertions and narrow explanatory prose to what is actually asserted. `CompositeDeviceMergerTests:67`
also says the single-interface SKY key is keyed by PID despite asserting its transport-shaped ID.
Reopen full merge test units, the guarantees pin table, and internal merge rationale after any rule/oracle change.

source_definition.text:
### CORE-A-C012 — Hardware-test descriptions exceed their actual oracles (documentation + test adequacy)

The integration files were read in full; none ran. `CompositeDiscoveryIntegrationTests:34–36` still
expects pre-Phase-2 red results. Its independent enumeration uses production transport enumerators and
a copied PID/name policy: it is independent of the merger, not an independent hardware census. Counts
by type cannot detect an equal-count substitution. The test claims allow-listed fixtures, yet several
cases enumerate/open every returned key directly. Describe the actual idle USB rig and ownership scope.

`DiscoveryUnattendedTests` says no applet session is opened. Its discovery still opens internal metadata
connections, selects Management for PC/SC, and can affect selection state on a shared/direct handle.
Its subset assertions constrain interface bits rather than prove membership inclusion; its initial
revision=1 checks assume no intervening publication. `YubiKeyTests.WaitForChangeAsync<DeviceAdded>`
can succeed on initial replay, so the current description does not prove a new insertion after a prompt.
The two stronger attended protocols assert removal/reinsertion plus final healthy stream completion,
but no execution proves a physical/native lane here. Their success-path pump waits also do not establish
failure-path pump drain. Preserve these as oracle/qualification limits, with any assertion/harness changes
in a separately authorized scope. Reopen test XML/comments, discovery hardware instructions, guarantee
test names, and historical evidence wording after harness changes or a new exact OS/device run.

### CORE-A-C013 — Shared fixture instructions still claim pre-operation hard failure (documentation)

Shared read: `YubiKeyTestInfrastructure.InitializeDevicesAsync` performs fresh All discovery, then a
live `device.GetDeviceInfoAsync()` before applying the allow list; it snapshots that separate live result
in `YubiKeyTestState`. It does not reuse `CachedDeviceInfo`. Nonmatches and read failures are filtered;
no authorized results return an empty list. `AllowList` exits only for an empty configured list with
unknown-serial authorization disabled. The README and contributor examples claiming exit on every
unauthorized serial and no hardware operation before authorization need precise distinctions between
read-only identification and test-body authorization. This observation does not authorize a new gate.

`IYubiKeyFilter` still shows nonexistent `YubiKeyTheory`/`YubiKeyTestDevice`; `YubiKeyTestState.Placeholder`
still describes re-enumeration rather than first-match lazy binding. The fixture cache remains run-local
and independent of one-shot manager evidence. Alias `management-001:MGMT-XREF-003` is a reopened
documentation dependency, not a newly counted runtime bug. Reopen these exact shared units and any
selected hardware authorization prose with the SHARED editor. Preserve earlier resolved applet prose.

### CORE-A-C015 — Development firmware behavior is SDK policy, not hardware fact (documentation)

`FirmwareVersion.cs:46–74` says every alpha/beta key is based on 5.8.0 or later and tells readers to
suspect the key rather than command encoding. The code only knows `Major == 0`; `FeatureTests` pins
optimistic acceptance even for 0.0.0 and arbitrary major-zero values. `Default` also represents unknown
0.0.0. State that compatibility policy, numeric ordering, and its inability to prove command support.
DeviceInfo may replace the behavioral version using a non-final qualifier; the supplied default version
otherwise wins over a well-encoded firmware TLV in C#, while the pinned Python parser prefers the TLV.
That cross-SDK precedence difference is implementation policy, not a wire violation by itself.
Reopen firmware/feature XML, metadata reference, and applet gate guidance after a policy or effective-version change.

### CORE-A-C016 — Metadata raw preservation requires a scoped design decision

`CreateFromTlvs` ignores unknown tags and preserves some unnamed enum values, but publishes no complete
raw response or unknown-TLV collection. Duplicate tags fail through `ToDictionary` with an ordinary
argument exception; the declared BadResponse condition is therefore not exhaustive. Unknown qualifier
types are retained numerically and treated as non-final. The root forward-compatibility doctrine asks
for raw response escape hatches where practical. Decide this metadata-specific representation and error
contract separately; do not add fields or reject open values during Pass 1. Reopen metadata construction
XML, Management returns, diagnostic examples, and cache equality after a decided representation change.

### CORE-A-C017 — Metadata cache does not carry the identity cache's PID qualification

`FindYubiKeys.ReadIdentityAsync` checks the cached PID before using identity. Its metadata cache instead
stores only `Info` and member interface IDs, and `PopulateMetadataAsync:443–446` reuses it without a PID
check. With a stable single FIDO interface ID changing from 0120 to 0402, neither PID needs serial
disambiguation, and the same metadata key can therefore reuse the old value without hotplug/absence.
The existing PID-change fault test deliberately forces the identity path with two OTP instances; it
does not check this metadata-only path. Normal platform reconfiguration often changes interface IDs,
so this is a source-visible conditional limitation, not a demonstrated hardware failure.

Classify this as an implementation candidate and a documentation qualification: the physical-model
statement that successful identity/metadata evidence expires on PID change needs to distinguish the
two caches. Reopen finder cache comments, physical-model discovery, cached-metadata troubleshooting,
and the PID-change regression description after a cache-validity decision or stable-ID test.
Coordinator experiment A-E04 can use one scripted interface, two known FIDO PIDs, a constant interface
ID, changed serial/capabilities, and no activity notification; add a hotplug invalidation control.
No experiment ran.

### CORE-A-C021 — Successful serial-less identity reads are cached despite retry prose

`FindYubiKeys.cs:84–86` says a serial-disabled read is absent from the identity cache and retried next
scan. `ReadIdentityAsync:380–381` actually caches every non-null DeviceInfo, including one whose
SerialNumber is null, and reuses it at 371–372 when the PID is unchanged. The guarantees guide at
39–44 likewise promises retries for null serials. Successful metadata without a serial is different
from an exception/timeout; the latter really is retried and has dedicated fault-injection assertions.
Those fake response helpers always encode a serial and do not test this successful-serial-less arm.

Record a documentation correction and an implementation-policy decision rather than assuming every
serial-less device should be reprobed forever. One-shot Find already uses fresh evidence. For an owned
monitor/finder, decide when a successful serial-less observation should expire, preserving conservative
grouping and native admission. Coordinator A-E06 can supply two same-PID scripted interfaces with
successful metadata omitting tag 02, count opens across scans, then provide serial-bearing responses
with and without an activity invalidation control. Reopen finder cache comments, guarantee convergence,
serial-latch XML, and troubleshooting when the caching policy or that oracle changes. No experiment ran.

The original clause defines PIV PIN **application** security status and its loss on application deselection, separately from Global PIN. It does not specify PC/SC handle/process isolation or the YubiKey PIN=ONCE policy. `PcscNativeResources.cs:118` says power-off ensures card-wide state cannot outlive this connection. `SmartCardSharingTests.cs:276–288` says the card is powered off so state cannot outlive the session; its only final assertion checks the fake's supplied `UNPOWER_CARD` argument. A borrowed session ends before its connection does, so even the named lifetime is too broad.

Supported direction: explain that strict PC/SC exclusivity limits other resource-manager clients, shared modes accept shared application state, and built-in release **requests** power-off and checks return statuses. Explain PIV application status with its actual selection conditions; reserve device-wide claims for measured vendor/platform evidence. `DefaultSharing` is initially Exclusive, while `default(SmartCardSharing)` is the zero-valued fallback enum member; docs should continue naming the factory policy explicitly.

**Original evidence:** `sources/register.md` (NIST original-PDF extraction; direct PDF blocked), PC/SC Part 5 §3.2.5.2 and Windows disconnect parameter/status documentation. **Actual oracles:** mode arrays, `IsExclusive`, native call counts, factory snapshot tests and requested release disposition. They establish managed selection and arguments, rather than a real competing process or physical power-state change.

**Required unchanged paths:** `SmartCardSharing.cs`, `PcscNativeResources.cs`, `SmartCardConnectionFactory.cs`, `ISmartCardConnection.cs`, `SmartCardSharingTests.cs`, Core README §PC/SC sharing policy, Core CLAUDE §Connection Factory Pattern; PIV README/CLAUDE/API state explanations and examples remain the later PIV boundary's review. **Migration:** preserve explicit Shared/fallback startup opt-in and snapshot timing. **Reopen trigger:** a sharing default, disconnect disposition, card-state statement or measured isolation result changes. ## CORE-B1-C002 — enumeration context cleanup starts too late

**Documentation:** candidate contract addition/qualification. **Runtime:** source-confirmed missing deterministic cleanup paths; Pass 2. **Policy:** deterministic enumeration ownership is the expected resource-management direction, rather than an authorized fix. **Qualification:** no native leak measurement.

`FindPcscDevices.FindAll`, lines 98–114, calls `SCardListReaders`, returns for non-success/empty results, deduplicates names and can log a warning before entering the `try/finally` at line 115. A successfully established context on those exits is left to SafeHandle finalization. A throwing list call, allocation or logger also bypasses the finalizer block. The ordinary no-readers path can repeat in every scan. In contrast, the recognized-USB return at line 134 occurs **inside** the finally and disposes its context.

The fix for `audit-v2-20261022-20261031:#18` owns reader-name allocation after line 136 and remains correct for that exact scope. This separate context gap must not undo that scoped resolution or silently broaden the old ID.

`FindPcscDevicesTests` often supplies an invalid default `SCardContext`; `PcscReaderNameOwnershipTests` checks `Context.IsClosed` only on paths that enter the finally. .NET 10 SafeHandle's managed closed state also does not prove a native ReleaseHandle succeeded. Public `IFindPcscDevices.FindAllAsync` currently supplies no useful XML describing its one-shot results, generic/NFC status probing or cancellation boundary: cancellation is checked before worker admission; once launched it awaits the worker without detaching. Higher-level finder budgets bound a different wait.

**Required unchanged paths:** `FindPcscDevices.cs`, `ISCardApi.cs`, `SCardContext.cs`, `SCard.Interop.cs`, `FindPcscDevicesTests.cs`, `PcscReaderNameOwnershipTests.cs`; Core discovery/ownership guides and module instructions where enumeration completion is explained. A owns discovery narrative integration; B4 owns native wrappers. **Reopen trigger:** move context ownership to cover every post-establishment exit, change unavailable-service/list-error policy, or change caller-wait behavior. Add counting-context fakes for non-success, empty and throwing ListReaders, warning failure and successful integrated-reader paths before physical leak qualification.

## CORE-B1-C003 — listener success path can repeatedly request immediate status

**Documentation:** candidate correction of timing rationale. **Runtime:** source/API-supported busy-loop candidate; no execution. **Policy:** maintain bounded failure cadence and event-hint role. **Qualification:** exact OS/native-shim behavior and call cadence need a bounded native lane.

`DesktopSmartCardDeviceListener.cs:318–332` creates new states for every wait and never preserves `EventState` as a later `CurrentState`. `SCARD_READER_STATE.Create` sets CurrentState to zero. PC/SC Part 5 §3.2.4 and pcsc-lite's original API define all-zero UNAWARE as an immediate status response. On successful reader listing/status calls the loop reaches its next iteration without a sleep. `WaitForPnpChange` also recreates zero PnP state; its concrete behavior requires OS qualification. The one-second parameter is a maximum wait and supplies no minimum delay for the ordinary-reader success path.

`DesktopSmartCardDeviceListenerSCardErrorTests` pins a single backoff before retry/reestablishment on **failure**; it supplies no quiet-success cadence oracle. The integration quiet-period test counts callbacks over 500 ms, rather than native call count or CPU consumption.

**Required unchanged paths:** listener source, `SCardReaderStates.cs`, `SCardState.cs`, `SCard.Interop.cs`, listener error/disposal/integration tests; Core listener/concurrency guidance and discovery guide timing statements. **Reopen trigger:** persistent state or explicit cadence enforcement changes; verify stable reader/PnP conditions independently on Windows, Linux and macOS. A consumes the listener-hint implications; B4 rechecks native layout/shim behavior. Avoid a portable CPU-rate guarantee based on fakes alone.

source_definition.text:
## CORE-B1-C004 — listener partial lifetimes and finalizer commentary need a precise bound

**Documentation:** candidate correction. **Runtime:** partial allocation and timeout/restart ownership candidates, Pass 2. **Policy:** maintain deterministic owner shutdown and avoid freeing active native resources. **Qualification:** no finalizer or held-native experiment executed.

- `WaitForPnpChange` allocates its name before a native call and frees it afterward without finally (`281–307`). A managed/native seam exception loses that allocation.
- `WaitForStatusChange` allocates ordinary names, then the combined array and PnP name **before** its finally (`318–326`). A later allocation failure leaves earlier owned names outside cleanup. The corrected `CreateMany` helper handles failure **within** its own allocation loop; it cannot protect subsequent caller allocations.
- `Start` records a context and catches startup/baseline failures without disposing partial state (`80–109`). Retry after Error can replace that context. `StopListening` clears `_listenerThread` before joining; on its eight-second timeout it clears `_context` and returns. `Start` can subsequently reset `_shouldStop` and install a new thread/context while the old thread is alive; the old loop reads shared mutable fields. Thus “bounded leak” describes one stop attempt, not a process-wide fixed resource bound or safe restart generation.
- The finalizer directly disposes `_context`; its XML says it ensures cleanup. A running ThreadStart retains the listener, so ordinary abandonment need not make it finalizable. `Finalizer_DoesNotThrowException` catches creation/start exceptions and only asserts that the GC calls returned without a caught exception. It neither observes finalizer entry nor proves context release/thread exit. A real exception on the finalizer thread would not be an ordinary exception caught around `GC.Collect`.

`PcscContextIsolationTests` is a useful fake oracle: cancel/release handles equal the monitor context, the held connection context remains distinct and unreleased, and transmit completes after the test opens its gate. That establishes call routing under the fake's cancel behavior. It does not establish a native timeout, all shutdown races or finalizer safety.

**Required unchanged paths:** listener source, listener disposal/error/integration tests, `PcscContextIsolationTests.cs`, native context/reader helpers, Core instructions and listener-facing API remarks. **Migration:** direct callers should set callbacks before Start, dispose explicitly and avoid lifecycle calls inside callbacks; monitor consumers keep the monitor as owner. **Reopen trigger:** atomic shutdown/restart-generation policy, actual late thread drain, partial-start cleanup or allocation ownership changes. Proposed tests must own a release gate in finally and observe actual old-thread termination before disposing fake events; the current tests must not be used as broad finalizer acceptance.

## CORE-B1-C005 — preserve the registered HID failure-release distinction

**Documentation:** candidate correction. **Runtime:** existing compatibility behavior, decision deferred. **Policy:** B4/maintainer must decide any future tightening for Windows/custom HID. **Qualification:** external/native behavior remains implementation-specific.

`RegisteredConnections.cs:21–26` promises teardown followed by lease release and finished teardown for every disposal call. SmartCard wrappers use `releaseLeaseOnFailure: false` plus quarantine; FIDO/OTP wrappers use the default `true` and release even if inner disposal throws. `DeviceConnectionRegistryTests.RegisteredFidoHidConnection_ExternalDisposeFailure_KeepsPriorLeaseBehavior` explicitly asserts `ReleaseCount == 1` after the exception. Built-in macOS/Linux slots bypass these wrappers and give the token to their native owner.

Supported direction: describe shared disposal **outcome**, preserve successful-teardown ordering, and name the failure-release policy for each route. A faulted disposal task is not generic native release proof. `DisposalGate` itself documents its configurable policy correctly; it is a useful unchanged dependency.

**Required unchanged paths:** registered wrappers, `DisposalGate.cs`, `DeviceConnectionRegistryTests.cs`, `HidConnectionSlot.cs`, `YubiKeyDevice.cs`, ownership/raw-tier guides and platform handoffs. **Reopen trigger:** Windows/custom HID gains checked release or wrapper policy changes. Shared editor should qualify `connection-ownership-and-contention.md:109–113`; B4 owns any native conclusion. No broad native HID audit was performed here.

source_definition.text:
## CORE-B1-C006 — transaction end completion and error reporting are distinct

**Documentation:** candidate contract clarification. **Runtime:** observed behavior; product decision if failure should be thrown earlier. **Policy:** scope error reporting needs maintainer adjudication. **Qualification:** native transaction/reset behavior remains OS-specific.

`PcscConnectionNativeState.EndTransaction` captures exceptions or status failure, sets EndFailed and closes the connection, but completes `EndCompletion` with a uint. `TransactionScope.Dispose/DisposeAsync` calls `reportEndFailure` on non-success. `UsbSmartCardConnection` supplies a Debug logger callback. Thus built-in scope disposal can return normally after native end **failed**, while the later connection disposal reports the stored error and checked resource cleanup still releases the claim if proven.

`AsyncTransaction_FailedAsyncEnd_RefusesFurtherWorkAndShutdownReportsFailure` awaits scope disposal without expecting a throw, then expects ObjectDisposedException on transmit and SCardException on connection shutdown. `EndFailure_StillReleasesNativeResourcesAndPhysicalClaim` asserts end/disconnect/context counts and successful reopen after the shutdown error. These are coherent, specific oracles. The title `AsyncScopeEndAwaitsNativeEnd...` actually holds a transmit before end; its fake end returns immediately, so that assertion does not independently hold native EndTransaction itself.

`ISmartCardConnection.cs:45–68` should explain the built-in outcome and asynchronous runtime cast pattern, while keeping custom default synchronous dispatch explicit. A transaction does not exclude other callers using the **same connection** between raw calls. Caller workflow serialization remains necessary. Windows' documented idle transaction reset and current SCARD_W_RESET_CARD semantics are platform conditions, not new portable SDK promises.

**Required unchanged paths:** interface, native owner, Usb facade, lifetime tests, Core README transaction example, raw-tier/ownership guides. **Migration:** retain IDisposable signature and conditional IAsyncDisposable disposal; any API/error policy change requires separate implementation authorization. **Reopen trigger:** scope disposal starts throwing native errors, transaction error state/recovery changes, or a new bounded held-end oracle is added.

## CORE-B1-C007 — reconcile active shared ownership claims with current routes

**Documentation:** candidate correction. **Runtime:** no new fix proposed here. **Policy:** keep known-member/process bounds and per-exchange exclusion. **Qualification:** later platform/session/wire packets must confirm their own tests.

`connection-ownership-and-contention.md:9–10` still suggests native PC/SC sharing violations ordinarily surface as SCardException. The built-in strict Exclusive route maps exactly that status to ConnectionInUseException with an inner SCardException; explicit Shared failures/custom providers can differ. `195–199` describes active disposal wake as macOS-only and says other built-ins receive no wake. Current `FidoHidProtocol` invokes `ITerminalWakeControl` and Linux FIDO implements that seam too; the raw-tier guide already says macOS/Linux. Reconcile this with B2/B5, rather than auditing all platform implementations from B1.

`Known bounds` says hotplug failure must be bounded and must not strand the lease. Current safety deliberately retains uncertain claims and permits indefinitely pending native work. State which managed waits are bounded, name unresolved native ownership and explain recovery rather than implying universal bounded teardown. `DeviceConnectionRegistry` introductory disposal wording and registered-wrapper wording need the same success/failure distinction.

Keep historical async plans historical: the old addendum's `DisposalGate` failure-release statement describes its then-current source. It must not be silently rewritten as an active contract. Test comments in `ApplicationSessionScpTests` and `ConnectionOwnershipContractTests` contain upstream/phase/Rust/Python comparisons; retain the local rationale but replace unsupported current-version authority with direct behavior. C's pinned Python register can settle a retained comparison later; no duplicate checkout was created.

**Required unchanged paths:** active ownership guide, raw-tier guide, Core README/CLAUDE, registry/wrappers, `ApplicationSession.cs` lifetime remarks (B5), the two named tests; historical plan sections retain provenance. Diagram SVG/PNG currently represent the happy ownership route consistently; treat them as candidate-associated unchanged simplifications, not complete error-state models. **Reopen trigger:** mapping, wake routing, claim quarantine or workflow guard boundaries change. The shared editor owns all shared-file edits.

source_definition.text:
## CORE-B1-C008 — make public callback ownership and CLI selection commentary actionable

**Documentation:** candidate enhancement/correction. **Runtime:** source behavior retained. **Policy:** caller ownership on success is required for the generic helper. **Qualification:** consumer-shape compilation remains assigned validation work.

`YubiKeyConnectionExtensions.CreateSessionOverTransportAsync<TResult>` disposes its created connection when the delegate fails. On success it returns TResult unchanged and never disposes the connection; built-in callers explicitly call internal `OwnConnection`. Public external delegates cannot call that internal method. XML should require the delegate's successful result to own/expose/dispose the connection and provide a complete ownership-bearing result example; simply constructing a borrowed session would leak the hidden connection. `SessionTransportTests...Succeeds_LeavesConnectionOwnedByResult` returns the connection itself and checks it was left open, rather than asserting an arbitrary result automatically owns it.

The assigned `YkCommandBase.AppletTransports` XML says the first type is auto-selected. Actual DeviceSelector uses the first type to **prefer a device** in noninteractive selection, while YkCommandBase forwards only the explicit requested transport into PreferredConnection. Explain device eligibility/preference separately from subsequent applet transport choice. The transport arrays match Core's documented defaults for the selected getter scope; whole applet command behavior belongs to later boundary packets.

**Required unchanged paths:** connection extensions, SessionTransportTests, CLI base, DeviceSelector and its tests (A), relevant raw-session/owned-result examples, Core ownership guide. **Reopen trigger:** public ownership-transfer capability or helper success/failure semantics change. The final report supplies a complete callback/result pattern for later compilation; it is not a product edit.

source_definition.text:
## CORE-B1-C009 — post-open slot logging can escape cleanup ownership

**Documentation:** candidate qualification of failure cleanup promises. **Runtime:** source-backed exceptional-path candidate, Pass 2. **Policy:** logger failure must preserve native ownership until actual release. **Qualification:** no injected log experiment executed.

`PcscConnectionSlot.OpenRegisteredConnectionAsync:68–74` awaits an already initialized registered connection, then logs Information before returning it. A throwing logger exits without disposing that returned local. YubiKeyDevice has already transferred registration ownership and deliberately avoids releasing it. Best-effort facade finalization is the remaining possible recovery, with no bound. In the **external factory** branch (`77–95`), an Information logger exception after successful open reaches the catch that releases registration without disposing the raw connection; that can permit reopen while the external resource is still owned. `OpenRawConnectionAsync:52–56` has the analogous undisposed local after logging failure.

`SmartCardConnectionFactoryTests` covers logger **creation before rooting** and Debug log failures inside `UsbSmartCardConnection.InitializeAsync`, whose catch drains native cleanup. Those assertions do not cover the slot's post-open Information logger. `SessionTransportTests` proves a cleanup-logger failure preserves an original factory failure, which is a separate call site.

**Required unchanged paths:** PC/SC slot, native factory/facade, YubiKeyDevice ownership catch, logging helpers (C), factory/lifetime/transport tests and factory ownership XML. **Reopen trigger:** post-open logger handling/cleanup changes; test both registered built-in and external-factory routes with a valid fake opened handle, assert cleanup order and no early claim release, and retain cleanup failures separately from the original logger exception.

## CORE-B1-C010 — PC/SC worker ambient context retention needs a scoped decision

**Documentation:** record only until intent is settled. **Runtime:** source-backed retention mechanism; no secret-retention finding claimed. **Policy:** ask whether PC/SC owner workers should suppress caller ExecutionContext as the newer HID owners do. **Qualification:** no runtime probe.

`PcscConnectionNativeState.EnsureWorker:228–239` uses normal Thread.Start; .NET 10 v10.0.0 Thread source captures ExecutionContext. A long-lived/rooted native owner can therefore keep ambient AsyncLocal state reachable independently of the caller's awaited method lifetime. This is separate from the safe lifetime of the explicitly borrowed command buffer. Existing worker tests assert one managed thread ID and native-call ordering; they do not assert ambient context isolation.

**Required unchanged paths:** native owner, Usb facade, lifetime tests, context-aware logging/presence ownership commentary and B2/B3 owner comparisons. **Reopen trigger:** approved suppression/isolation policy or a documented reason to preserve flow. A bounded nonsecret AsyncLocal sentinel experiment may later distinguish captured state from caller input; retain platform and full API context and avoid recording actual secrets.

## CORE-B3-C006 — macOS worker context flow extends B1's decision

**Documentation:** record-only pending policy. **Runtime:** source-visible ExecutionContext capture.
**Decision:** extend `CORE-B1-C010`, nonadditively. **Qualification:** no AsyncLocal experiment.

FIDO `ScheduleLocked:288–291`, OTP `ScheduleLocked:105–108` and listener `Generation:341`
start ordinary Threads without suppressing flow. The pinned .NET 10 Thread source retained by B1
captures ExecutionContext at Start. These rooted long-lived workers can therefore retain caller
ambient state. Linux's separate suppression policy is a comparison point, not automatically a Mac
requirement. This concerns ambient state, not ownership of a passed connection, prompt, or report copy.

**Oracles:** worker identity assertions establish one worker; they contain no ambient-state assertion.
**Unchanged review set:** two owners, listener, their lifetime tests, logging/presence context guidance
(C/B5), B1-C010 and B2 policy comparison. **Reopen:** selected context-flow policy or explicit nonsecret
AsyncLocal probe. Coordinator must decide whether to consolidate all three routes under B1's question.

## CORE-B1-C012 — whole-scope immediate refusal has a discovery-wait precedence bound

**Documentation:** candidate precision improvement. **Runtime:** current sequential acquisition, decision if stronger immediate refusal is required. **Policy:** preserve sorted acquisition/rollback and waiting-connection priority. **Qualification:** source trace only.

`DeviceConnectionRegistry.AcquireConnectionAsync:110–114` acquires members sequentially. Concrete trace: discovery holds `a`; a live connection holds `b`; a new connection asks for `[a,b]`. It waits for discovery on `a` before inspecting the already-held `b`. Consequently the remarks saying any known-member conflict is refused **immediately** need this local condition, and “atomic” should mean a logical registration with rollback rather than an indivisible dictionary-wide transaction.

Existing `AcquireConnection_LaterMemberHeld_RollsBackEarlierClaims` has a free first member, and `AcquireConnection_DiscoveryOnMember_CancellationRollsBack...` has a held **later discovery** member. Neither asserts the discovery-first/live-later trace. The implementation correctly sorts/deduplicates IDs and prevents double successful overlapping ownership; this candidate does not allege two live winners or deadlock.

**Required unchanged paths:** registry XML, `DeviceConnectionRegistryTests.cs`, ownership architecture §One physical device and §Discovery coordination, Core concurrency guide, IYubiKey.ConnectAsync XML (A). **Reopen trigger:** full-scope preflight/admission policy or wait precedence changes. A deterministic test should hold a discovery `a` and connection `b`, observe the wait, cancel it and prove no native open and complete rollback; any stricter refusal requirement is a separate runtime decision.

## CORE-B2-C001 — lead Linux setup with scoped device access

**Documentation:** candidate correction, consequential security guidance. **Runtime:** unchanged.
**Decision:** choose documented desktop/session or administrator-managed service access, keeping the
application's deployment context explicit. **Qualification:** no rule was installed or evaluated here.

`docs/linux-setup.md:54–87` leads with `MODE="0666"` for every Yubico hidraw interface and every Yubico USB
device, then makes `0660` group access an alternative at 89–102. This grants access to every local user;
the USB rule is broader than the hidraw access these transports require. PC/SC uses its daemon/reader
driver path, described separately at 5–38. Existing package rules may already provide appropriate access.
The supported next step is to inspect the selected YubiKey node and distribution-supplied rules, then
grant access only to the intended user/group or active desktop session. A service needs an explicitly
managed group rather than an assumed interactive login ACL. Explain that `plugdev` is an example group
which the administrator must provide, and keep read/write requirements near the actual typed opens.

Original systemd 262 `udev(7)` defines OWNER/GROUP/MODE and rule matching; pinned Yubico Device Permissions
separates PC/SC, keyboard and FIDO access. The linked upstream `69-yubikey.rules` currently assigns
`ID_SECURITY_TOKEN`, rather than the guide's world-writable modes. That rule alone is not proof that
every distribution grants an ACL: the administrator must verify the resulting access in its deployment.
Those publications are configuration/API guidance, not a normative SDK permission mandate.

**Source → oracle → documentation:** owner `Open` uses O_RDWR; descriptor discovery can fall back to
O_RDONLY; `IsHidrawReady` only probes read access. Fake open flags and descriptor tests establish arguments,
not user ACL behavior. Reopen Linux setup, root/Core prerequisites, native-AOT deployment guidance and
direct-report examples together when permission guidance changes. Keep `LinuxHidInterface.cs`,
`LinuxHidEventSource.cs`, both native owners and `LinuxHidReportApi.cs` as associated unchanged dependencies.
**Trigger:** permission defaults, required access flags, distribution rules or PC/SC prerequisites change.

## CORE-B2-C002 — distinguish stage history from current integration ownership

**Documentation:** candidate current-context clarification. **Runtime:** unchanged. **Decision:** retain
stage records as historical evidence, with a precise successor pointer rather than rewriting old results.
**Qualification:** original execution identities remain attached to their own source revisions.

`linux-hid-routing.md:45–48,102–105` attributes discovery scheduling/lease transfer to ProtocolDeviceInfo.
The current split places it in `SharedDeviceInfoRead.ConnectAndReadAsync:248–292`; ProtocolDeviceInfo
borrows an open connection and owns only its matching protocol. The L5 text is useful history, but a
reader using it as current architecture needs the current actor and source pin nearby. Similarly,
`LinuxDescriptorLease.cs:19–21` and `LinuxHidEventSource.cs:192–193` speak of a future reactor even though
the production reactor now retains registration-long references. Replace active comments with the
present two reference scopes. Stage documents contain compressed forms such as `at most32`, `holds160`,
`exactly8` and `report length or64`; normal spacing improves those explanations without changing meaning.

The L0/L1/L2/L3/L4 and L6a statements excluding later-stage work are **historical slice scopes**. Preserve
them with that status. The latest `linux-native-acceptance.md` checkpoint at 12:39:27Z records serial 103
and passing read-only physical routes; its earlier blocked sections and original JSON fields stay intact.
Current PublicSyncBoundaryRegistry requires 23 entries, including eight Linux entries; L6a's recorded
24 describes its earlier source. Adapter links are reachability/runnable-test links rather than recursive
execution or native release attestation. Do not silently change historical counts to current counts.

**Source → oracle → documentation:** SharedDeviceInfoRead transfers before invoking open and releases
only an untransferred lease. LinuxDiscoveryAdmissionTests holds PID admission through actual owner close;
LinuxHidRoutingTests supplies direct/composite/epoch cases. Read-only hardware checkpoint and integration
native-only output have distinct envelopes. Reopen the L5 handoff, active Core guides, native lifetime
comments, architecture ownership/raw tiers and migration notes after a responsibility split or new current
qualification. Associated unchanged paths include all L0–L6 evidence documents/JSON, the actual slot,
SharedDeviceInfoRead, ProtocolDeviceInfo, both owners and all 14 verifier files. Preserve old source/hash
identities and explanatory limits. B1-C007 supplies the separate active ownership-guide Linux wake correction.

ABI failure or authorized declaration change. **Decision:** any executable return-type alignment is Pass 2.
**Qualification:** source contracts checked against systemd v257, not every deployed libudev build.

`Udev.Interop.cs:123–129,164–171,192–199` describes returned native strings as ASCII, while the managed
Linux `PtrToStringAnsi` conversion uses UTF-8. These are native NUL-terminated strings copied while their
udev/enumerate/device owner remains live. Name that representation and lifetime instead of promising
ASCII-only paths. `238–246` states the C signature of `udev_monitor_unref` as `void`; the original v257
implementation returns a monitor pointer, documented always NULL. The managed `void` import ignores that
return, so a comment fix can state the actual C contract while preserving executable tokens.

Parent lookup is borrowed from the child, as v257 `libudev-device.c:388–415` explicitly states. Current
GetList/ReceiveEvent scopes retain the child while traversing/copying. The overloads using DangerousGetHandle
have narrower caller-owned lifetime obligations than SafeHandle-marshalled calls; no parent SafeHandle or
extra unref should be invented. Release of a monitor reference owns its socket cleanup, distinct from
checking a hidraw physical connection claim.

**Source → oracle → documentation:** LinuxUdevHidEventSourceTests checks the signed get_fd delegate shape
and scripted wake policy, not the native unref signature or non-ASCII path round trip. Reopen Udev.Interop,
the four udev SafeHandles, LinuxHidInterface/EventSource, native rationale and relevant Linux setup text if
encoding or reference ownership changes. Add a non-ASCII scoped path-copy probe only in a later assigned
native environment. All those paths remain unchanged here. B4 retains general loading/marshalling claims.

## CORE-B2-C004 — unversioned libudev name adds an undeclared runtime prerequisite

**Documentation:** candidate installation/troubleshooting qualification. **Runtime:** source/package-backed
deployment candidate. **Decision:** select a stable soname or an explicit resolver in separately authorized
implementation work; avoid ad hoc user-created library symlinks. **Qualification:** no clean Ubuntu host
or container was executed in B2.

`Native/Linux/Linux.Libraries.cs:20` imports `libudev.so`. Canonical's Ubuntu noble amd64 file lists place
`libudev.so.1` and `.1.7.8` in `libudev1`, while the unversioned `libudev.so` is in `libudev-dev`. .NET's
documented Linux name variations add prefixes/suffixes; they do not infer `.so.1` from `.so`.
`FindHidInterfaces.FindAllLinux:81–91` catches DllNotFoundException, logs a warning and returns no HID
interfaces. A runtime-only installation can therefore look like empty discovery despite valid device
permissions. Existing setup prerequisites describe PC/SC packages and udev rules without this loader-name
condition. The conditional conclusion applies when the unversioned entry/resolver is absent; the package
lists do not prove every Ubuntu machine has that condition.

**Source → oracle → documentation:** injected report/reactor tests bypass libudev resolution; the retained
Omarchy native/selected-key captures qualify that recorded host, not a minimal Ubuntu package set. Reopen
Linux setup, Core/root requirements, native-AOT packaging, empty-discovery troubleshooting and native
library-name comments after the selected loading contract changes. Keep Linux.Libraries, Udev.Interop,
FindHidInterfaces and verifier publish/project contracts as associated unchanged dependencies. B4 receives
the loader/package boundary, while A receives the warning-versus-empty-discovery consequence. A meaningful
future test uses an isolated minimal deployment with recorded installed files and library resolution;
it should assert discovery's classified outcome independently of attached hardware.

## CORE-B2-C005 — successful-path oracles leave some assertion-failure lifetimes undrained

**Documentation:** candidate qualification of test-coverage descriptions. **Runtime:** test-harness cleanup
candidate, separate from shipping owner correctness. **Decision:** repair cleanup only under an explicit
test-edit scope, preserving existing assertions. **Qualification:** source traces only, no injected red run.

`LinuxFidoHidConnectionTests.Open_ReturnsInvocationWhileNativeIsHeld:23–36` drains the invocation in
finally, then awaits/disposes the returned connection outside it. If AssertResponsive throws, release can
finish a successful open but control skips disposal of that result. The rooted native owner/worker can
remain live. `HeldWrite...:39–70` similarly drains output in finally but only requests disposal inside the
successful assertion body. A failure before that request leaves the connection owner unclosed. In
`CancelDuringPreparation:95–117`, a pre-cancellation assertion failure can make finally's expected-cancel
assertion replace the primary error after a successful open. The OTP held-native helper at 23–40 instead
captures and disposes the opened result within finally and is a useful local pattern.

`LinuxHidRoutingTests.DiscoveryTimeout...LateOpenAndCleanup:154–190` releases its gate in finally but does
not independently await late work/recovery on every failing branch. Some reactor tests create/publish a
held poll token and make setup assertions before a cleanup finally; `PublishedFailedAdmission:38–80` is a
concrete example. A harness watchdog bounding a child limits test-process damage, while actual resource
drain must still be observed for any cleanup claim. Later worker-failure setup and direct synchronous
disposal witness already have stronger finally/independent-join cleanup; preserve those positive oracles.

**Source → oracle → documentation:** stage descriptions say tests cover named outcomes, which remains
true for their successful paths. Avoid upgrading those descriptions into arbitrary setup/assertion-failure
or all-race guarantees. Reopen these complete test methods, their fakes/WithheldNativeProbe, L0 helper
contract, L3/L5/L6a evidence summaries, boundary registry links and Core test guidance when cleanup changes.
LinuxNativeAbiTests and Python gate tests also prefer literal `/tmp/opencode` when it exists; the current
quota-constrained coordinator must prepare a home-backed adaptation before executing those selections.
Their temporary-path behavior is a separate harness constraint, not an owner leak diagnosis.

## CORE-B2-C006 — expose direct Linux report ownership and parser scope at the entry point

**Documentation:** candidate XML usefulness/precision improvement. **Runtime:** unchanged.
**Decision:** retain public synchronous compatibility signatures and expert responsibility.
**Qualification:** examples remain source-checked, `VALID-NOT-CHECKED` for later consumer compilation.

`LinuxHidInterface.ConnectToFeatureReports/ConnectToIOReports:126–142` only promises an active connection.
The implementation synchronously waits for a new native owner; the caller owns the returned connection,
these direct opens carry no grouped registry claim, input IO waits indefinitely, and feature calls wait
for native return. Keep this concise ownership/blocking context near these implementation comments and
the public IHidInterface contract (B4/B1 dependency), with the typed `IYubiKey.ConnectAsync<T>` alternative
and explicit `await using` ownership. Detailed facade XML already accurately distinguishes metadata,
actual input length, typed64/8 versus bounded direct SET and checked close.

`ParseHidDescriptorBytes:328–367` extracts the first Usage Page/Usage independently and returns the pair;
`GetList:111–115` applies supported vendor/interface classification. The prominent validation comment at
330–331 should name this downstream validation rather than imply a general HID parser or in-method
combination validator. The complete descriptor vectors explicitly characterize truncation, long-item
progress, first-pair selection and narrowed values; LinuxHidReportSizes separately rejects numbered
reports and bounds widened report arithmetic. Preserve those deliberate limits.

**Source → oracle → documentation:** direct facade tests assert supported caller lengths and actual
read count; routing tests prove typed opens select owners; raw factory initialization/recovery belongs
B5. Reopen LinuxHidInterface, IHidInterface/IHidConnection XML, raw-access architecture, Core README direct
examples and migration EOF/no-timeout notes if direct access or descriptor classification changes.
LinuxHidIOReportConnection, LinuxHidFeatureReportConnection and both typed connections are useful
associated unchanged paths. B5 retains CTAPHID/OTP wire semantics and applet-specific recovery policy.

## CORE-B3-C001 — macOS status names and numeric values

**Documentation:** supported correction. **Runtime:** enum constants need separately scoped correction.
**Decision:** retain numeric native diagnostics and permission-specific advice. **Qualification:** no native run.

`docs/architecture/connection-ownership-and-contention.md:248` calls `0xE00002E2`
`kIOReturnNotOpen`. Apple's `xnu-12377.1.9` `IOReturn.h:160,183` assigns NotOpen to
`0xE00002CD`, and NotPermitted to `0xE00002E2`. Keep the old observed numeric error and history;
correct its interpretation. `IOHIDDeviceClass.m:496–552` at `777ccd9698845aadf711e32d843c8c9b777431d9`
returns NotPermitted when TCC authorization is required and denied. That is one supported cause,
rather than proof of the cause on the historical host. Replug advice alone is insufficient for a
permission refusal: inspect the exact host/application Input Monitoring authorization and preserve
the complete diagnostic. Fresh-host permission behavior remains user-deferred.

`src/Core/src/Native/MacOS/IOKitFramework/IOKitFramework.Interop.cs:90–127` increments across
reserved 0x2CB and 0x2DC, and gives Invalid the next sequential value rather than 0xE0000001.
Consequently CannotLock onward has wrong values (one then two positions low). Current packet code
uses only `KERN_SUCCESS`; FIDO/OTP exclusive-open handling explicitly uses correct 0xE00002C5.
This establishes a latent definition defect and misleading diagnostics, rather than a demonstrated
wrong live branch. `source-checks.json` records a static comparison, with no C# type initialization.

**Oracles:** existing fake tests inject raw status integers and check hex text/cleanup; none compare
the whole enum to Apple's constants. **Unchanged review set:** enum, troubleshooting unit, `IIOKitDeviceLifetime.cs`,
FIDO/OTP owners, feature/IO facade and route tests, Core platform troubleshooting/setup guidance.
**Reopen:** numeric definitions, error translation, permission findings or recovery advice changes.
The SHARED editor owns the guide; a later implementation owner fixes numeric definitions and adds
an independent constant vector without invoking native libraries.

**Qualification:** no native run.

`docs/architecture/connection-ownership-and-contention.md:248` calls `0xE00002E2`
`kIOReturnNotOpen`. Apple's `xnu-12377.1.9` `IOReturn.h:160,183` assigns NotOpen to
`0xE00002CD`, and NotPermitted to `0xE00002E2`. Keep the old observed numeric error and history;
correct its interpretation. `IOHIDDeviceClass.m:496–552` at `777ccd9698845aadf711e32d843c8c9b777431d9`
returns NotPermitted when TCC authorization is required and denied. That is one supported cause,
rather than proof of the cause on the historical host. Replug advice alone is insufficient for a
permission refusal: inspect the exact host/application Input Monitoring authorization and preserve
the complete diagnostic. Fresh-host permission behavior remains user-deferred.

`src/Core/src/Native/MacOS/IOKitFramework/IOKitFramework.Interop.cs:90–127` increments across
reserved 0x2CB and 0x2DC, and gives Invalid the next sequential value rather than 0xE0000001.
Consequently CannotLock onward has wrong values (one then two positions low). Current packet code
uses only `KERN_SUCCESS`; FIDO/OTP exclusive-open handling explicitly uses correct 0xE00002C5.
This establishes a latent definition defect and misleading diagnostics, rather than a demonstrated
wrong live branch. `source-checks.json` records a static comparison, with no C# type initialization.

## CORE-B3-C002 — enumeration dereferences a possibly null copied set

**Documentation:** qualification candidate. **Runtime:** source/API-supported unsafe native argument path.
**Decision:** select empty-versus-error handling separately. **Qualification:** no empty-host native reproduction.

`MacOSHidInterface.GetList:65–72` passes manager and `IOHIDManagerCopyDevices` results onward without
null checks. Apple's pinned `IOHIDManager.c:1136–1152` initializes the copied set to NULL and returns
it when `manager->devices` is absent. `CFSet.h:309–317,390–404` requires a valid CFSet; invalid arguments
have undefined behavior. Thus an empty/unavailable device set can reach `CFSetGetCount(0)`, outside
its contract. The listener's `GetInitialEntryIds:408–427` already handles a null set separately.
Do not describe a guaranteed managed exception or guaranteed crash; the OS behavior remains unexecuted.

**Oracles:** packet lifetime tests inject owners, not enumeration. `FindHidInterfacesBoundaryTests`
(B4) gates a supplied enumeration delegate and supplies no null-CFSet oracle. **Unchanged review set:**
`MacOSHidInterface.cs`, CFSet/manager declarations, `FindHidInterfaces.cs` (B4), discovery setup and
no-device troubleshooting (A/SHARED), scan boundary tests. **Reopen:** acquisition null guards,
empty-result policy or enumeration failure handling changes. A future narrow fakeable scan seam or
supervised empty-Mac host can verify this; a Linux build is irrelevant to the native condition.

## CORE-B3-C003 — integer-property XML names the wrong exception

**Documentation:** supported correction. **Runtime:** preserve current behavior pending any separate policy.
**Decision:** document absent versus lossy-conversion outcomes. **Qualification:** source only.

`IOKitHelpers.GetIntPropertyValue:35–46` declares NullReferenceException but deliberately accesses
`Nullable<int>.Value`. Absence produces InvalidOperationException. Its nullable sibling returns null
for a missing property, throws PlatformApiException on a different CF type and returns zero if
`CFNumberGetValue` reports a lossy/out-of-range conversion. Apple's `CFNumber.h:111–123` says a best
conversion is written even when false is returned; the wrapper discards it. XML should expose these
wrapper outcomes and avoid implying every query requires an already-open device: enumeration queries
properties before device open. No new conversion policy or validation is authorized.

**Oracles:** CoreFoundationString tests establish UTF-8 bytes/encoding/null creation, not numeric-property
exception behavior. **Unchanged review set:** helper, `CoreFoundationString.cs`, CFNumber imports,
interface enumeration and lifetime GetIntProperty callers. **Reopen:** exception, absent-property,
numeric-conversion or pre-open-query policy changes. A static Nullable contract citation and a later
pure injected property vector can settle the public commentary without device work.

## CORE-B3-C004 — callback rationale predates the rooted listener generation

**Documentation:** supported correction, with a dormant-boundary warning. **Runtime:** current active
listener route is rooted; old array-registration surface remains risky if reused. **Decision:** retain
or remove that unused seam in a separately authorized scope. **Qualification:** generated stubs uninspected here.

Core `CLAUDE.md:488–495` describes `_arrivedCallbackDelegate`, `_removedCallbackDelegate`,
`_abandonedCallbackDelegates` and a zero context. None exists in the pinned listener. `StartGeneration:79–83`
passes static Cdecl UnmanagedCallersOnly addresses and `generation.Context`; Generation roots itself
with GCHandle before registration. Rewrite the instruction around the actual context and native drain.
This shared passage is a secondary handoff to B4/SHARED, outside B3's five assigned shared IDs.

`IIOKitDeviceLifetime.RegisterInputReportCallback` and its native import still accept `byte[]` storage
for an asynchronous registration. The current active persistent FIDO route instead allocates the report
buffer in the native backend and roots only managed callback context. An ordinary call-scoped array pin
would be insufficient if the old registration method were revived without an enclosing persistent pin.
Repository usage search found no production call to that lifetime method outside its forwarding definition.
Record this dormant hazard without alleging a current active buffer-use-after-free.

**Oracles:** listener fakes invoke the static unmanaged address through a Cdecl delegate; native route
host wraps real callbacks and observes callback exit/close/unschedule/release order. Fake tests supply
no generated-marshaller or deployed OS proof. **Unchanged review set:** Core CLAUDE, listener, IOKit
callback declarations, lifetime seam, listener tests and `ListenerDrainScenario.cs`, FIDO bridge.
**Reopen:** callback ABI, GC root, retained input pointer, scheduling mode or registration usage changes.

## CORE-B3-C005 — partial listener startup has permanently retained paths

**Documentation:** retain the conservative quarantine rationale, qualify completeness. **Runtime:** partial
allocation cleanup candidates. **Decision:** distinguish intentional post-registration retention from
unnecessary pre-registration loss. **Qualification:** source only; allocation/start faults unexecuted.

`StartGeneration:73–92` obtains a manager before constructing Generation. If construction throws before
assignment, the catch has no local cleanup for that manager. Generation allocates its GCHandle before
constructing Thread (`335–342`), so failure during Thread construction can also leave its new root.
After `RegistrationAttempted=true`, any registration or `Thread.Start` exception intentionally retains
the rooted generation. With an unstarted thread, Stop returns at 107 and restart is refused at 54;
there is no late worker to perform cleanup. That is safety-biased retained uncertainty, not successful
teardown or the ordinary callback-timeout/late-drain recovery tested elsewhere.

`StartGeneration` also uses an unguarded Error logger in its catch. A throwing logger can bypass its
remaining pre-registration Cleanup/Status assignments; `HotplugSignals` may still attempt disposal,
which cannot clean an unstarted generation. Keep diagnostics failure distinct from native failure.

**Oracles:** listener tests cover held callbacks, shared timeout budget, unschedule/release failure,
normal restart and thrown/nonzero manager Open/Close. None injects Generation/Thread construction,
register/start failure or start-catch logger failure. **Unchanged review set:** listener/Generation,
listener tests, Core listener guidance, monitor HotplugSignals (A), real drain host. **Reopen:** startup
ownership, explicit registration proof, no-thread cleanup or logger-failure handling changes. Preserve
rooting after ambiguous registration until a separately proved quiescence path exists.

## CORE-B3-C007 — direct IO reads preserve fixed FIDO framing, not arbitrary descriptor-sized input

**Documentation:** qualify expert-facade input semantics. **Runtime:** current behavior is deliberately
asserted; no change selected. **Decision:** any future generalized raw descriptor input is separate.
**Qualification:** fake-native source oracles and historical selected-key evidence remain distinct.

`MacOSHidIOReportConnection` reports native InputReportSize/OutputReportSize, forwards arbitrary SET
lengths, but Receive shares FIDO `Owner.Report:419–442`: exactly 64 bytes are accepted; 65 bytes with a zero leading
report ID are stripped to 64 bytes; any other frame terminalizes. `MacOSHidIOFacadeTests.ReportsUseNativeDescriptorSizesAndFixedFidoPackets`
asserts metadata sizes 65/72, SET lengths 72/empty and GET length 64 from a 65-byte input. Explain this near direct-report guidance so a
descriptor-size property is not mistaken for the actual returned buffer length. The six-second timeout
detaches only the waiting reader; native owner/input continues. Feature expert GET separately returns
the original eight-byte array and zero-pads successful short GETs, whereas typed OTP rejects short GET.

**Unchanged review set:** both expert facades, both owners, IO/feature facade and compatibility tests,
Core README direct access, raw-tier synchronous table, IHidConnection XML (B4), migration examples.
**Reopen:** normalization, accepted frame shape, direct GET length or typed/expert split changes.
Fresh editor should retain the accurate timeout/SET/caller-owner material and add the missing nearby
input qualification rather than replacing it with a universal raw-HID contract.

## CORE-B3-C008 — native source and runtime evidence need explicit versions

**Documentation:** qualification candidate for future publication. **Runtime:** native protocol source
located and read; no new native defect or runtime acceptance allocated. **Decision:** source publication
and package build provenance remain a release question. **Qualification:** exact current binary build
correspondence and fresh Mac execution remain open.

The published 1.18.1 source at `dedba95b94946907112a7953cd82df8a15c22655` provides `owner.h/c`,
`internal.h`, `backend_iohid.c` and `native_exports.c`. It explicitly distinguishes acknowledgment/drain
from checked destroy. Destroy accepts success, or narrow removed/drained NoDevice and confirmed-service-
termination BadArgument cases, and permanently retains unknown close failures. Managed WaitShutdown
accepts OK/FAULT as quiescence; only successful Destroy frees the GCHandle context. The caller separately
releases its IOHIDDevice creation reference. Native report slots are freed, not explicitly zeroed: managed
copy clearing supports no end-to-end secret-erasure claim.

The cached package nuspec gives version 1.18.1 and repository URL, without a source commit. Source blobs
match the published release tree; that establishes source identity, not a reproducible build mapping to
the cached dylib. Preserve a precise binary/source-provenance qualification until producer evidence binds it.
Historical `.8` macOS 15.7.7 arm64/.NET 10.0.12 serial 31683481 firmware 5.7.4 results remain original-revision
results. The current integration compiled route/comparison hosts on Linux using canonical 1.18.1 under
its explicit three-property profile. It neither ran them on Mac nor changed comparison defaults.

**Oracles:** `MacOSHidInputVerification` exercises a nonshipping synthetic experiment ABI, not the
shipping package; fake bridge CloseFault=6 probes managed policy. Route host checks actual production
type/selected-serial responses and borrowed reuse, and explicitly treats watchdog kill as OS cleanup.
`CurrentProfile` separates process allocations/CPU, native-only unavailability, fixture firmware absence,
loaded-path absence, partial samples and source/build correspondence. Preserve those honest bounds.

**Unchanged review set:** all three verification hosts/projects, Core macOS lifetime guidance, historical
architecture/AOT evidence, package/loader declarations (B4), raw tier/setup/migration summaries. **Reopen:**
native package/export/source version, native close proof, OS floor, runtime profile or actual Mac results
changes. Keep old cold-start before/after mode (`.8` and two exact commits) distinct from current `--profile`.
Future complete source publication should include producer commit, artifact/package hashes, native deployment
floor and a typed borrowed-connection example; source access alone is not device qualification.

## CORE-B3-C009 — CFNumberType's native width is implicit/mismatched

**Documentation:** ABI rationale candidate. **Runtime:** declaration-width discrepancy for separate review.
**Decision:** exact native type carriers should follow headers. **Qualification:** no call corruption alleged.

`CoreFoundation.Interop.cs:67,81` declares `theType` as int for CFNumberCreate/GetValue. Apple's
`CFNumber.h:49` defines CFNumberType as `CF_ENUM(CFIndex, ...)`, and `CFBase.h:380–390` makes CFIndex
a signed long on Apple LP64. The declarations therefore use 32 bits for a native 64-bit type. Current
callers pass only positive 3, so this source-level discrepancy does not demonstrate a failing live call.
Keep the four-byte **value storage** for kCFNumberSInt32Type separate from the enum's parameter width.
The other reviewed synchronous CFIndex/report length carriers are long; Boolean has explicit U1.

**Oracles:** string byte tests and injected integer-property returns bypass these imports. **Unchanged
review set:** CF imports, IOKitHelpers, listener vendor dictionary, original CF headers and later generated
stub/native ABI validation (B4). **Reopen:** native carrier types, architecture targets or generated call
evidence changes. A later reviewer should inspect actual stubs/ABI on supported Mac architectures before
describing a physical effect; avoid an unqualified statement that every imported signature already matches.

## CORE-B4-C001 — Windows compatibility lifetime and early claim release

**Documentation:** describe Windows' actual synchronous compatibility route beside
the macOS/Linux owner routes. **Runtime/policy:** extend `CORE-B1-C005`
nonadditively to a successful Dispose while synchronous native I/O is still active.
**Qualification:** pending on every Windows architecture/device lane.

`HidConnectionSlot.OpenRawConnectionAsync:82–85` creates the synchronous report
connection before Task.FromResult. `FidoHidConnection.SendAsync/ReceiveAsync` and
`OtpHidConnection.SendAsync/ReceiveAsync` call SetReport/GetReport inline and ignore
their token. `WindowsHidReportAccess:214–224` opens FILE_FLAG.NORMAL; ReadFile and
WriteFile at 155/183 use a null OVERLAPPED pointer. There is no baseline
CancelIoEx/GetOverlappedResult import, native-pending request object, native I/O
admission gate, shared disposal task, or checked-close outcome in that owner.

A synchronous native call borrows SafeFileHandle through its generated marshaller.
.NET 10 SafeHandleMarshaller.ManagedToUnmanagedIn takes DangerousAddRef and releases
it on Free. Calling `_handle.Dispose()` at WindowsHidReportAccess:316 during a held
ReadFile can close managed admission while deferring the actual native close to
the last reference release. Windows report facade Dispose/DisposeAsync simply
forwards this call. RegisteredFidoHidConnection and RegisteredOtpHidConnection use
DisposalGate's default lease-on-failure policy; after the inner Dispose returns,
the registration can be released while the other thread is still in native I/O.
On a custom adapter's throwing Dispose, B1-C005's unknown-release case also applies.
The built-in path's missing release observation and the custom path's arbitrary
teardown contract remain distinct. Protocol guard drain can protect a correctly
owned session exchange, but direct raw calls and connection disposal on another
thread still need their own contract.

The SafeHandle protects the active native handle from premature physical close;
its protection does not extend the registry token automatically. This is a
source-backed ordering concern, not a captured Windows race. A caller's task
submission, method invocation return, actual native terminal status, reference
drain and release proof must be recorded separately in future tests.

**Current oracles:** WindowsHidConnectionOpenFailureTests asserts a fake report
owner was disposed when open throws, and was retained after successful feature
open; it exercises no blocked native call or native close. PublicApi adapter tests
remain B1's read oracle for forwarding/copy cleanup, rather than Windows native
acceptance. No current assertion read here establishes the early-release case.

**Reopen:** WindowsHidReportAccess; both Windows report connections; the two typed
compatibility adapters; HidConnectionSlot; RegisteredConnections and DisposalGate
(B1); IFidoHidConnection/IOtpHidConnection/IHidConnection/IHidInterface XML (B5/B4);
Core README/CLAUDE, raw-access-tiers, connection-ownership-and-contention and the
adapter/public-sync registries. A new Windows owner, admission rule, actual
cancellation implementation or checked native release requires a focused delta.
Retain accurate existing Windows/custom limitations until that evidence arrives.

## CORE-B4-C002 — Listener shutdown proof, partial startup and disposed restart

**Documentation:** qualify callback/finalizer assurance and timeout-test commentary.
**Runtime:** preserve native registration/context/delegate through actual successful
unregister; refuse Start after disposed. **Policy:** choose quarantine/retry on
unregister failure separately. **Qualification:** pending Windows native fault lane.

WindowsHidDeviceListener.Stop:139–145 and Dispose(false):297–305 ignore
CM_Unregister_Notification's CONFIGRET and free the GCHandle regardless. Microsoft
documents that unregister waits for pending callbacks, prohibits calling it from
the callback, and reports success versus CR_* failure. Success therefore supplies
the native drain relevant to releasing callback state; simply invoking it supplies
no successful-unregister observation. Restart after such an error discards the old
registration identity. Start:59–125 has no disposed check: Dispose sets `_disposed`
and suppresses finalization, but a subsequent successful Start can allocate a new
registration that a later Dispose's early-return path leaves live. This conflicts
with IDeviceChangeListener.Start's ObjectDisposedException contract.

The weak GCHandle allows the target to disappear before finalizer unregister.
The static callback drops a collected target, but GCHandle recovery/Target access
and its diagnostic log precede the try at line 168; the catch's log can also throw.
Containment of all managed exceptions crossing the unmanaged callback boundary
needs its own evidence. A failed Start's logging paths can likewise throw before
ClearRegistrationState. These are failure-path candidates, not a claim that normal
successful CM registration leaks or that all finalizers are unsafe.

**Current oracles:** CfgMgr32InteropTests checks 416 bytes on any host; its Windows
case asserts Started then Stopped using the real OS. WindowsHidDeviceListenerTests
checks bounded UTF-16 parsing only. HidDeviceListenerDisposalTests accepts Error
after Start, and its two asynchronous disposal cases only compare Task.WhenAny's
winner without awaiting the disposal task. The integration disposal case also
checks status, but never awaits that task's result. These can miss a fast fault;
their time budget bounds the test's wait, rather than proving native drain or
cleanup after a failing assertion. No finalizer/failed-unregister assertion is
present in these read files. The quiet test's zero events also succeeds if Start
failed, so it establishes no successful native registration by itself.

**Reopen:** Windows listener, native CM unregister declaration/comments,
HidDeviceListener and IDeviceChangeListener lifecycle XML, the four named listener
test files, Core listener guidance, ownership guide and A's monitor teardown
explanation. Preserve parsing tests' precise and useful bounded-buffer oracle.
