original_index.desired: Keep honest current limitations and classify caller input, owned scalar/shared-secret copies, public points and key handles by semantic role. Track implementation cleanup and constant-time policy separately; remove the unsupported no-added-exposure rationale.
original_index.confidence: high-static; native allocation internals and exploitability unqualified
original_index.final_observation: Pinned .NET v10.0.0 EccSecurityTransforms routes absent Q through ExtractPublicKeyFromPrivateKey, whose ReadEncryptedPkcs8 replaces an ECParameters value containing a private D; that new managed array is not cleared by the runtime method. The supplied-Q path skips that derivation and ImportKey returns its CryptoPool staging in finally. ECDsaSecurityTransforms signing uses the imported SecKey and does not itself call the absent-Q extraction path. ECPrivateKey's assertion that supplied Q necessarily uses the same derivation path is unsupported by this checked revision. Narrow the warning to the verified D-only route; current installed runtime/native provider cleanup remains separately unqualified. source_definition.heading: Separate crypto-object disposal from all-buffer cleanup

original_index.title: Separate crypto-object disposal from all-buffer cleanup
original_index.observed: AesUtilities creates plaintext.ToArray copies and MemoryStream buffers without clearing them; decrypt returns another copy while its MemoryStream retains plaintext. The byte-array overload clones a returned ReadOnlyMemory again. X963Kdf retains the secret-derived stack hash on return and lacks cleanup for partial result on failure. CmacPrimitivesOpenSsl.CmacFinal leaves outputBuffer on success/failure, although the active default is the managed AesCmac implementation. ASN private encoders use AsnWriter buffers in addition to the owned encodings they explicitly clear.
original_index.desired: Keep current cleanup evidence local to each owner. Track unzeroed owned copies in Pass 2. Qualify docs/CRYPTO-APIS.md's blanket zero-allocation/auto-zeroing claims: disposing a provider does not clear caller arrays or every temporary copy.
original_index.confidence: high for explicit SDK copies; AsnWriter/provider internals need exact revision follow-up
original_index.final_observation: Exact AsnWriter v10.0.0 source confirms Encode returns an independent copy without clearing the writer buffer and Reset clears the written internal prefix. Production private encoders omit Reset even though some test fixture writers use it. Existing zeroing observers establish explicit INTEGER/encoded temporary cleanup, not writer-storage erasure. BCL/provider disposal cannot erase every caller/runtime copy. CmacPrimitivesOpenSsl is a retained alternate helper and is not the active ICmacPrimitives default. HsmAuth's two RNG allocations precede the inner try; second allocation failure can abandon the first owned key. No failure injection ran.

original_index.ownership_qualification: ReadOnlyMemory is not an immutable-storage or clearing-owner contract. Tlv.Value and key getters borrow their owners; Memory-returning TLV helpers transfer writable output. DecodeDictionary transfers values typed ReadOnlyMemory without a disposable clear owner, and clearing a later mutable copy does not erase the original or abandoned parse copies. The raw HID paragraph likewise cannot make original readonly returned secret storage disappear by clearing a copy. Preserve this as a caller/API ownership qualification for C005/C006/C013 and the B5 boundary; recommend existing disposable/writable owners where available, without inventing a breaking API or writable-cast workaround. For C017, retain the contributor policy favoring disposable reference-type owners while correcting its rationale: a struct copy duplicates an array reference, not the array bytes, so clearing the shared backing array affects all aliases. The hazard is shared mutation and ambiguous lifetime/disposal ownership, not an inability for ZeroMemory to reach aliases. The root CLAUDE wording is a narrow shared-editor dependency, not an added C primary population.
original_index.allocation_failure_qualification: For C013, RSAParameters.DeepCopy allocates several private arrays in an object initializer before NormalizeParameters enters its try. Failure of a later allocation can abandon earlier owned private clones without explicit clearing; observer-throw fixtures occur after that allocation stage and do not cover it. This is a conditional source-derived lifetime concern, not an executed OOM repro, exploit claim or authorization for a refactor.

source_definition.heading: Retain current catalog mappings while qualifying registry status

original_index.title: Retain current catalog mappings while qualifying registry status
original_index.observed: The fetched IANA COSE registry (updated 2026-08-25) confirms all inspected catalog numeric mappings, including Ed25519 -19 and Brainpool 256/258/259. Its Recommended column labels ES256/384/512, EdDSA, RS1 and AES-CBC deprecated; this is separate from the catalog's structural applicability and existing applet profile choices. CoseKeyType cites the Common Parameters registry while linking the key-type subregistry. Unknown/None zero values are local sentinels in registries where zero is reserved.
original_index.desired: Use precise registry names and local sentinel semantics. If adding registry status context, state it as registry metadata and retain existing protocol profiles. Do not automatically replace ES256/EdDSA IDs in CTAP/WebAuthn or infer provider/device support from a registered mapping.
original_index.confidence: high registry-row inspection; protocol policy remains with boundary owners
original_index.final_observation: All modeled curve/key/operation rows inspected against current IANA records and original RFC/SEC tables. RFC 9053 allows ECDSA only for its modeled P-256/P-384/P-521 set unless extended elsewhere; broad structural ECDSA applicability on secp256k1/Brainpool does not validate its associated -7 mapping for that combination. SEC 2 retrieved v2.0 copy retains Draft page headers; identify those exact bytes instead of upgrading its status. The NIST final metadata was readable through webfetch, while direct PDF and follow-up retention requests were forbidden; no NIST-final table or approval claim is inferred.

original_index.ownership_qualification: ReadOnlyMemory is not an immutable-storage or clearing-owner contract. Tlv.Value and key getters borrow their owners; Memory-returning TLV helpers transfer writable output. DecodeDictionary transfers values typed ReadOnlyMemory without a disposable clear owner, and clearing a later mutable copy does not erase the original or abandoned parse copies. The raw HID paragraph likewise cannot make original readonly returned secret storage disappear by clearing a copy. Preserve this as a caller/API ownership qualification for C005/C006/C013 and the B5 boundary; recommend existing disposable/writable owners where available, without inventing a breaking API or writable-cast workaround. For C017, retain the contributor policy favoring disposable reference-type owners while correcting its rationale: a struct copy duplicates an array reference, not the array bytes, so clearing the shared backing array affects all aliases. The hazard is shared mutation and ambiguous lifetime/disposal ownership, not an inability for ZeroMemory to reach aliases. The root CLAUDE wording is a narrow shared-editor dependency, not an added C primary population.

{
  "id": "CORE-C-C020",
  "kind": "cross-packet-ownership-documentation-and-policy",
  "title": "Make SCP parameter containment ownership visible to B6 and applet editors",
  "observed": "The narrowly read parameter boundary differs by layer: SessionCreationOptions borrows SCP parameters and presence service; Scp03KeyParameters stores the supplied StaticKeys reference and disposes that same object; StaticKeys clones source spans. Scp11KeyParameters copies the certificate collection but retains each certificate and the EC private-key reference, then disposes those same objects. Its public key is retained without disposal. Record with-expressions can share the contained disposable owners. XML calls OceKeyRef required for a/c although the constructor does not require it, and claims empty/null b fields while the full constructor accepts supplied values for b.",
  "desired": "B6 should describe construction/containment/disposal and alias lifetime explicitly, and reconcile required-versus-optional metadata with its actual SCP initializer. Cross-reference the same ownership in Security Domain/OpenPGP/PIV examples. Keep record cloning and disposed-alias policy as consequential decisions rather than changing APIs in Pass 1.",

      "path": "src/Core/src/Protocols/SmartCard/Scp/Scp03KeyParameters.cs",
      "first": 25,

source_definition.heading: Make SCP parameter containment ownership visible to B6 and applet editors

original_index.title: Make SCP parameter containment ownership visible to B6 and applet editors
original_index.observed: The narrowly read parameter boundary differs by layer: SessionCreationOptions borrows SCP parameters and presence service; Scp03KeyParameters stores the supplied StaticKeys reference and disposes that same object; StaticKeys clones source spans. Scp11KeyParameters copies the certificate collection but retains each certificate and the EC private-key reference, then disposes those same objects. Its public key is retained without disposal. Record with-expressions can share the contained disposable owners. XML calls OceKeyRef required for a/c although the constructor does not require it, and claims empty/null b fields while the full constructor accepts supplied values for b.
original_index.desired: B6 should describe construction/containment/disposal and alias lifetime explicitly, and reconcile required-versus-optional metadata with its actual SCP initializer. Cross-reference the same ownership in Security Domain/OpenPGP/PIV examples. Keep record cloning and disposed-alias policy as consequential decisions rather than changing APIs in Pass 1.

## X001 — Bound connection exclusion to observed membership

**Documentation:** qualify `src/Ctap2/README.md:306–310` and `src/Ctap2/CLAUDE.md:47–50` with
SDK-managed opens and the member interfaces Core actually grouped. The README's “all of its interfaces”
can imply coordination between independent disjoint discovery scopes. Core's process-local registry
coordinates overlapping known member IDs. A's accepted-evidence limitations also retain possible
partial-evidence cross-key grouping. An applet choosing HID first supplies no stronger physical proof.
**Implementation:** reuse A/B1 mechanisms; no new registry defect allocated. **Policy:** retain existing
grouping/selection policy. **Qualification:** external processes, direct factories and disjoint scopes
need their own coordination. Reopen these two guides, `S/IYubiKeyExtensions.cs`, discovery/physical-model
and raw-tier guidance after changes to member identity, grouping, direct-open admission or no-fallback.

## X002 — Keep complete workflows alive through their actual final continuation

**Documentation:** retain the existing command-adjacency qualifications in `S/ICtap2Session.cs`,
`S/CredentialManagement/CredentialManagement.cs` and `S/LargeBlobs/LargeBlobStorage.cs`. Add the
public-workflow disposal scope alongside general session lifetime advice if X001 is edited.
`ApplicationSession.cs:43–44,470–568` and `ExchangeGuard.cs:49–62` protect an admitted protocol exchange,
then detach/release; they supply no whole-workflow lease. CTAP decode/logging and terminal notification
can continue after that exchange exits. Credential enumeration, ClientPin GetInfo/key-agreement/token
requests and blob read-modify-write each span several admissions. **Implementation:** source-visible
boundary, shared with B5-C006; a workflow lease/reentrancy design needs separate authorization.
**Policy:** caller serializes and fully awaits the workflow, then disposes; callbacks should return
promptly and leave disposal to the enclosing owner. **Qualification:** the held Linux/Mac tests exercise
one exchange, not every post-exchange continuation or interleaving schedule. Reopen the named helpers,
session XML, both module guides, interaction/raw-tier guidance and cross-layer tests if workflow admission,
post-exchange ownership or disposal behavior changes. Do not prescribe an invented SDK lease helper.

## X003 — Preserve CTAP-XREF-003 and the PIN input allocation decision

Aliases: `ctap2-001:CTAP-XREF-003`, `ctap2-001:CTAP-IMP-006`,
`openpgp-001:PGP-CORE-001`; shared C001–C004 concerns remain C-owned.
**Documentation:** `S/Credentials/Ctap2CredentialOptions.cs:24–40` already states UTF-16 counts and
the UTF-8/code-point/NFC/final-NUL distinction. Retain it. Core options XML needs its C-owned units
explained; this boundary contributes the actual CTAP call site. `FidoPinHelper` uses Core's reader,
whereas WebAuthn's separate prompt contract carries explicit units. **Implementation:** ClientPin
`ValidatePin:571–584` checks only 4–63 bytes; Core first counts `char` values and then encodes.
**Policy:** decide where strict UTF-8, normalization checks, code-point/device minima and final-NUL
validation belong. Avoid silently normalizing an existing credential. **Qualification:** ASCII fixtures
leave multibyte and surrogate behavior open. Reopen the preset, Core reader/options, ClientPin parameters,
FidoPinHelper and both layer guides after enforcement or units change. OpenPGP retains its own profile;
its shared alias confers no CTAP rules on PW1/PW3.

source_definition.text:
## X004 — Track each response owner rather than clearing one convenient view

Aliases: `ctap2-001:CTAP-IMP-027`, related `webauthn-001:WA-IMP-006/013`.
**Documentation:** current response/extension XML and README correctly disclose the separate copies.
**Implementation:** HidBackend transfers a status-stripped view of Core's accumulated array;
SmartCardBackend transfers a view of `ApduResponse`'s copied data. Typed make/get decoders create
authData, largeBlobKey and other independent arrays; make retains attestation/unsigned slices of its
input. AuthenticatorData creates another raw array and an ED suffix. Session disposal clears none of
these successful returned copies. Decode failure after backend transfer also leaves those lifetimes
outside backend cleanup. `StoredCredentialInfo.Decode` instead creates a private response clone,
clears that clone on failure/disposal and exposes largeBlobKey as a slice; the borrowed original survives.
**Policy:** design one coherent explicit owner/view/transfer contract, preserving valid unknown response
data. **Qualification:** `StoredCredentialInfo_Dispose_ZeroesOwnedViewsAndKeepsPublicFieldsUsable` checks
actual retained clone views and unchanged source; it supplies no transport/failure-clone observer.
Reopen all response/AuthenticatorData/attestation/extension owner XML, stored/enumeration models,
S/ICtap2Session.cs, both guides and WA result/PRF/blob consumers after ownership changes. B6 must separately
account for transport/APDU/SCP intermediate owners and APDU-error responses.
source_definition.heading: X004 — Track each response owner rather than clearing one convenient view

## X005 — PIN cryptographic exceptional cleanup remains local

Alias: `ctap2-001:CTAP-IMP-005`. **Documentation:** retain V1/V2/helper cleanup bounds.
**Implementation:** V1 Authenticate's stack full MAC lacks finally clearing; V1/V2 Decrypt can abandon
their allocated output after transform failure; PerformEcdhKeyAgreement derives Z before allocating its
public dictionary. Encapsulate's finally starts only after that helper returns. These are separate
failure sites, rather than one generic Core crypto defect. **Policy:** clear actual SDK-owned arrays on
every exit; provider/internal erasure requires separate evidence. **Qualification:** no provider/crypto
execution occurred. Reopen `S/Pin/PinUvAuthHelpers.cs`, both protocols, security notes and hmac-secret/PRF
callers after each selected site's repair. C's generic private-key/native cleanup concerns stay distinct.

## X006 — PIN peer labels are a CTAP profile boundary

Alias: `ctap2-001:CTAP-IMP-007`. **Documentation:** retain the explicit gap in helper and COSE guides;
“strict checks remain” in a high-level catalog passage means the required target, not proof they all run.
**Implementation:** helper validates X/Y byte-array type/32-byte width, forces BCL P-256 import and
delegates point validation, while omitting peer kty=2/crv=1/alg=-25 and optional-label restrictions.
No call to `Algorithms.FindForKey`, Core COSE metadata or generic CoseKey decode supplies those checks.
**Policy:** keep unknown response carriers open while validating security-critical PIN peers strictly.
**Qualification:** import errors can occur outside the helper's derivation catch. Reopen PIN/Encapsulate,
COSE/forward-compatibility XML, both guides and actual peer fixtures after profile validation changes.
source_definition.heading: X006 — PIN peer labels are a CTAP profile boundary

## X007 — ARKG wire profile and Core mathematics have separate authorities

Aliases: `ctap2-001:CTAP-IMP-029`, `ctap2-001:CTAP-DEC-003`; Core C018/C019 remain their own concerns.
**Documentation:** preserve draft-10's -65700 erratum and explicit experimental status. **Implementation:**
CTAP dispatches on alg before kty, reconstructs padded EC2 coordinates without checking nested curve,
and emits kty=2 plus byte-string-wrapped maps. Core Derive validates actual P-256 points and ctx <= 64,
but that mathematical boundary cannot recover the original labels or validate the chosen seed profile.
**Policy:** maintainer selects the pinned vendor/draft profile before changing encoders. **Qualification:**
Core cites expired draft-09 mathematics; CTAP cites expired draft-10 representation. Full equivalence,
Rust generator pin and actual NativeShims producer/provider evidence remain explicit gaps. Reopen
S/Cose, S/Arkg, previewSign generated/derived key types, Core ARKG rationale and both layer draft claims
after a selected profile or mathematical revision; preserve all frozen originals.

## X010 — Unsigned output support retains the old dropped-output identity

Aliases: `audit-v2-20261022-20261031:#4`, `ctap2-001:CTAP-IMP-030`,
`webauthn-001:WA-IMP-017`. **Documentation:** current get/make field tables accurately distinguish key 8
versus key 6 and incomplete outer-envelope preservation. **Implementation:** get skips key 8; make retains
modeled unsigned values as slices. Core CTAPHID/APDU preserves transport payload, not a CTAP model API.
**Policy:** select supported extension/raw escape hatch with X004 ownership; optional direct-largeBlob
support is a separate choice. **Qualification:** old tested-device absence and API removal give no
key 8 handling evidence. Reopen response raw/unsigned XML, extension codecs, forward-compatibility guides
and WA largeBlob processing only after support/ownership changes.

## X011 — Structural and conditional response checks stay with CTAP

Alias: `ctap2-001:CTAP-IMP-028`. **Documentation:** preserve declared ED/AT/count/key-length/full-envelope
limitations. **Implementation:** AuthenticatorData copies the ED remainder without one-map exhaustion;
make lacks AT enforcement; get casts uint32 count to int. Generic framing guards validate their own
length/CID/sequence domain; they supply no model/request/version validation. **Policy:** distinguish
standalone full-envelope checks from nested-reader consumption and request-conditioned checks.
**Qualification:** no parser change or new execution. Reopen the actual parsers, flags/count/extension
XML, model fixtures and WA recovery consumers after each selected validation change, keeping defects
separate even where they share the same model.
source_definition.heading: X011 — Structural and conditional response checks stay with CTAP

source_definition.text:
## X012 — Blob numeric ranges and cap are independent policy questions

Alias: `ctap2-001:CTAP-IMP-037`. **Documentation:** retain signed-Int64/read-cap/reconstruction bounds.
**Implementation:** blob origSize/key parsing uses signed ranges; decrypt skips above 1 MiB while encrypt
has no matching cap. Unknown encoded slices have a separate preservation lifetime. Core APDU/HID length
limits neither choose this cap nor promise a transaction across fragments. **Policy:** select numeric/raw
preservation and symmetrical/asymmetrical cap behavior. **Qualification:** no arbitrary-foreign-client
or whole-array atomicity claim. Reopen LargeBlobData/Storage, SpecFormat tests and both layer storage
guidance when the range/cap/preservation target changes.
source_definition.heading: X012 — Blob numeric ranges and cap are independent policy questions

## X014 — hmac-secret salt input has an independent failure scope

Alias facet: `ctap2-001:CTAP-IMP-035`, related `webauthn-001:WA-IMP-013`.
**Documentation:** retain ExtensionBuilder's intermediate-copy qualification. **Implementation:**
BuildHmacSecretInput allocates saltData then calls Encrypt/Authenticate without a cleanup finally;
an authentication failure can abandon encrypted output too. **Policy:** assign DTO/builder/result owners
without conflating salt authentication with token authorization. **Qualification:** PRF decoder clearing
its aggregate plaintext leaves its range/result copies separate. Reopen builder/HmacSecretInput,
PrfCodec/PrfOutput, both guides and real array-observer assertions after salt/result cleanup changes.

## X015 — Encrypted metadata needs an explicit protocol-wrapper choice

Aliases: `ctap2-001:CTAP-IMP-043`, cleanup facet `CTAP-IMP-035`.
**Documentation:** retain IV-only/arbitrary-block acceptance, opaque state and unauthenticated wrong-token
qualifications. **Implementation:** metadata uses BCL HKDF/AES directly, not Core catalog enforcement;
DeriveKey and failed plaintext allocation/transform have separate cleanup scopes. **Policy:** choose
strict GetInfo wrapper versus generic helper; token persistence/permissions remain ClientPin/authenticator
responsibilities. **Qualification:** a byte-equality test with opaque state neither authenticates the
token nor proves persistent-token issuance. Reopen decrypt/DeriveKey/GetInfo fields, two-session fixtures
and WA callers when length/token/cleanup behavior changes.

Alias: `ctap2-001:CTAP-IMP-004`. **Documentation:** preserve WithBytes/WithEncodedValue private-copy and
WithValue deferred-read descriptions. **Implementation:** Build clears Encode's intermediate array;
captured copies and CborWriter internal storage remain separate. Make/Get clear the final encoded
request in finally, while ClientPin/admin helpers have additional request copies. Raw SendCborRequest
borrows its supplied request; Core report copying never erases it. **Policy:** choose explicit builder
ownership/reset semantics, keeping raw API callers responsible for their borrowed input. **Qualification:**
no end-to-end erasure inference from one cleared array. Reopen builder/raw API, PIN/admin/extension callers,
security examples and WA-IMP-013 dependencies after copy-lifetime changes.

## X017 — Distinguish all firmware observations and configuration policy

**Documentation:** Ctap2Session factory XML accurately places the gate before the override. Retain that.
Core A-C015/B5-C001 own optimistic major-zero wording. CTAP CLAUDE's “treated as modern” should use the
same policy vocabulary when edited. **Implementation:** HID INIT caches vendor bytes separately;
Ctap2Session takes GetInfo's packed low-24-bit interpretation, or 0.0.0, then applies the override only for
Configure/SCP/session FirmwareVersion. Future GetInfo queries do not update it. **Policy:** preserve
capability/configuration/token/device checks beyond nominal thresholds. **Qualification:** Management
5.8.0, CTAP 0.0.1 and effective override are distinct evidence. Reopen factory/feature/GetInfo XML,
transport tests, Core FirmwareVersion and both guides after gate/provenance/config changes. B6 must settle
major-zero ForceShortApdus handling before any claim that a caller's short-APDU option always applies.

## X018 — Carry B5 framing/cancellation recovery into actual CTAP calls

**Documentation:** retain CTAPHID command versus CTAP operation/status distinction and valid-terminal
drain conditions. **Implementation:** backend sends unmasked CBOR 0x10; Core sends CANCEL once after an
observed keepalive, then drains the original response. Raced CTAP success is SDK policy; encoded 0x90's
late-success test differs from normalized-command matching. Malformed control lengths/reserved assigned
CIDs/partial failure without recovery latch remain distinct B5-C002/C003 mechanisms. **Policy:** dispose
and reopen after uncertainty instead of promising universal reuse. **Qualification:** no keepalive/no
terminal response can leave the task pending; physical cancellation and OS abort are separate observations.
Reopen backend/interface/session cancellation XML, cross-layer tests and raw-tier guide after any B5
framing/cancel/reset decision. These mechanisms are reused, not newly counted defects.

## X020 — Keep response cleanup reachable when diagnostic callbacks fail

**Documentation:** qualify the universal failure-cleanup sentence in CTAP CLAUDE:344–345 if this candidate
is accepted. Ordinary terminal-callback failure already has actual response-array assertions.
**Implementation:** both backends await final ResolveAsync before zeroing untransferred response.
On a CTAP failure, a throwing terminal callback is caught by UserPresenceNotification and logged; a
throwing logging provider there can escape before backend zeroing. This conditional diagnostic-failure
path is separate from X004 successful-response ownership and X005 crypto cleanup. **Policy:** decide
whether cleanup/primary-exception preservation must survive logger failure; route shared notification/log
behavior to C, local finalization structure to CTAP. **Qualification:** no new sentinel test ran and the
existing backend tests use ordinary logging. Reopen notification/Backend failure XML, module presence
claims and actual-buffer observers after this exceptional-path choice. Do not claim a reproduced leak.
source_definition.heading: X020 — Keep response cleanup reachable when diagnostic callbacks fail

## CORE-SD-X001 — Put effective version beside SCP11 creation and preserve reset provenance

**Observed:** SD `InitializeAsync:165–205` passes override or 5.3.0 to Core; `ScpInitializer:64–85` gates SCP11 at 5.7.2. README `126–135` shows generation then says to supply SCP11 parameters later, without the required override beside that task. Generation can reach a newer device without explicit version, while the subsequent SCP11 factory fails locally. Reset `765–799` drops original config/version and reuses retained parameters. SCP11 reset can therefore fail with wrapped NotSupported after SELECT but before PSO/authenticate; SCP03 can reauthenticate only with still-valid keys and loses config/explicit-version state. This refines SD-DEP-003 / SD-IMP-005 and B5-C001, without a new Core gate finding.

**Documentation:** expand README `126–152` with a typed complete creation scope using the known version; add immediate version condition to factory remarks (`SecurityDomainSession:125–130`, extension `35–41`) and contributor initialization `130–147`. Preserve already-accurate reset/Generate qualifications in interface `207–214,316–330`, README `177–182,202–207`, contributor reset `89–93`. Their unchanged outcome is retain with the more precise local pre-wire failure rationale.

**Runtime:** local omitted reset options remain source-confirmed; no fix. **Decision:** retain/redefine reset config/version/parameter reuse and failed-reinit lifecycle separately. **Qualification:** caller version is supplied policy, not hardware detection; major-zero policy and ForceShort behavior retain A/B6 ownership. Test helper's fresh factory reapplies version, so existing hardware calls do not prove option preservation.

**Reopen when:** reset option retention, Core setup gate or version policy changes. SHARED editor owns `SessionCreationOptions` XML, Core session/firmware guides, `docs/migration/v1-to-v2.md:119–120,822–826`; SD editor owns task snippets and test version/reset descriptions. No migration map API signature change is currently justified.

## CORE-SD-X002 — Make retained parameter and contained-object lifetimes actionable

**Observed:** SD `_scpKeyParams:83,94–101` retains exact caller object for reset. Core StaticKeys clones source; Scp03 parameters retain/dispose exact StaticKeys; Scp11 parameters copy only list and dispose private-key/certificate identities. Record cloning shares those owners. SD private import `608–617` reads caller key parameters without claiming them. README `217–225` correctly says borrowed and caller cleanup, but “what they own” leaves the SCP11 certificate/private-key identity transfer too implicit for a reusable provisioning flow. Inline default parameters in actual integration callers are not disposed by the helper. Associated aliases: SD-DEP-002, SD-IMP-008, B6-C007 and C-C020.

**Documentation:** add contained-object table/action near README security notes and SCP11 roles, contributor `123–128`, factory remarks; show a/c parameter scope enclosing every session with one private-key/certificate owner. Keep rotation `93–103` unchanged: it already disposes copied StaticKeys and clears source material in finally. Keep private-import XML `185–189` and local `613–614` comment: caller key ownership is accurately stated.

SD also leaves `SessionCreationOptions.UserPresencePrompt` unused: its constructor calls the base overload with no prompt. Keep the module's current no-prompt statement; refer generic “a session retains the service” XML in `SessionCreationOptions:25–28,58–60` to C/SHARED for an adoption condition rather than implying SD retains that service.

**Runtime:** alias disposal and local temporaries remain separate scopes. `SecurityDomainKeyMaterial:37–60,68–107` clears pooled plaintext, but leaves stack KCV/secret-derived AES output and allocated encrypted values with separate lifetimes; public-key/cert/serial metadata is not automatically sensitive. `PutEcKeyAsync:650` passes uninitialized `stackalloc byte[1]` as curve parameter. This extends SD-IMP-008's local cleanup/source-quality map, not a claim of observed garbage or a B6 crypto failure. **Decision:** contained-owner API policy, wrapper sharing and exact cleanup should be selected with B6/C. **Qualification:** provider-hidden storage and native erasure remain unproven.

**Reopen when:** parameter clone/disposal, reset retention, key export/import buffers or owned test inputs change. SD editor covers README/contributor/private-import explanation and helper comments; Core B6/C own parameter/key XML and record mechanism. Exact integration/fake paths and reasoned unchanged outcomes are in the file ledger; fixture/test cleanup needs separately authorized executable work.

## CORE-SD-X003 — Preserve the response owner distinction at the ROM facade

**Observed:** SD helper `816–823` returns response.Data, losing its supported clear handle. The ROM keeps the copied owner alive after session disposal; caller copy cleanup cannot reach it. GET DATA forwards caller requestData and object low bytes; caller must preserve input until the actual operation ends. KCV response and generic caller-encoded GET DATA may be sensitive, whereas listed references, CA IDs, public certificates and generated public points have different classification. B6-C002 owns transport/fragment/decrypted temporary copies. SD-DEP-004 and SD-IMP-008 preserve this applet consequence.

**Documentation:** enrich interface GET DATA `35–52` with input/result lifetime, actual Le semantics and absence of complete secret-clear ownership guarantee. Explain in README constraints/security notes that ROM return is neither a pool loan nor automatic erasure on disposal. Preserve certificate XML `76–92`: it already gives independent caller disposal and trust conditions. Its source cleanup resolution remains separate.

**Runtime:** no facade Clear API or zeroing fix is authorized. **Decision:** choose public owned-response/caller-copy/internal parser cleanup policy before claiming successful generic secret-result erasure; do not recommend unsafe writable casts. **Qualification:** clearing a final ApduResponse would clear status too, so inspect status first, and would still leave earlier copies scoped to B6. Current tests verify bytes, not post-use zeroing of these owners.

**Reopen when:** response/result representation or parser cleanup changes. Both facade/interface result XML, Core response/TLV ownership reference, SD key helpers, examples and test buffer observers need fresh review. `KeyInfo`/`CaIdentifier` XML remains unchanged: these are parsed metadata carriers, not sensitive response owners or trust proofs.

## CORE-SD-X004 — Treat partial raw reset as its own lifetime and recovery boundary

**Observed:** SD `765–936` lists keys through guarded protocol, then bypasses it for raw attempts. It clears flags only after all attempts and synchronous protocol disposal. Cancellation/ordinary repeated errors or diagnostic/disposal failure before that boundary can leave old flags/graph despite partial mutation or plaintext SCP termination. Reset's later reinit lacks Create's failure-dispose catch. Multi-exchange CA retrieval/reset is not serialized by one public-operation lease. SD-IMP-001/005, SD-DEP-004 and B5-C006 retain primary mechanisms.

**Documentation:** keep existing destructive/no-rollback/attempt-limit text; add nearby failed-reset disposal/reopen guidance to README reset `172–182`, interface Reset `316–330`, contributor reset `76–99`, test reset explanations. Clarify `SecurityDomainSession:788` “reset complete” as attempts finished, not observed restoration. Preserve helper two-session pattern: it disposes the reset session before the test session and reapplies original options.

**Runtime:** no changed retry/result/terminal-session behavior. **Decision:** whole-reset admission, readiness invalidation before raw work, incomplete-result reporting and failed reinit cleanup require maintainer selection. **Qualification:** at most 65 attempts is no wall-clock bound; native dispatch/drain/release remain distinct. Serial 125's 6A88 setup failures supply no reset execution. **Reopen when:** raw reset admission/status handling, flags, retained keys, reinit/disposal or vendor restoration evidence changes. SHARED editor rechecks raw-tier/disposal/cancellation wording; SD editor rechecks both Reset contracts and every helper/cleanup comment. `docs/AI-DOCS-GUIDE.md:484–509` already accurately qualifies destructive reset; retain unless those facts change.

## CORE-SD-X005 — Keep selected error wrapping and diagnostic provenance precise

**Observed:** SD selection precedes its Configure catch; only Apdu/BadResponse/NotSupported with parameters wrap. Core CLA-not-supported creates a nested NotSupported; immediate SD StatusWord is consequently null. Missing DEK InvalidOperation and provider errors escape. `SecureChannelException:70–74` embeds immediate inner.Message; SD GET DATA/import/generate/reset catches log full exception objects (`242,487,569,668,872`). Static logger selection is global. B6-C014/C-C008 own logging policy; this packet supplies actual SD provenance. Registry's SD-DEP-005 claim that formatter traces expose APDU data is stale: current formatter implementations have no logging, ordinary PC/SC trace logs headers/length only.

**Documentation:** existing selected-wrap XML and migration `822–826` are accurate and stay unchanged. Add useful diagnosis distinctions (local gate versus card status, nested status versus immediate, dispose/reopen after uncertainty) near contributor error/logging sections, not a broad “safe to log exception” promise. Keep key-reference logging snippet unchanged: values logged are metadata only. **Runtime:** unwrapped provider/InvalidOperation and raw-reset retry behavior are observations, not selected intended redesign. **Decision:** exception-text/provider redaction policy belongs to C/SHARED; no automatic removal of diagnostic detail. **Qualification:** no provider/plugin log capture ran and no real key was logged.

**Reopen when:** catch set, nesting, logger templates or provider policy changes. Both factories, `SecureChannelException`, contributor diagnostics, README constraints/security, `docs/migration/v1-to-v2-map.yml` scalar `securitydomain-exception`, and migration prose need simultaneous re-review. No current map edit is warranted; preserve unrelated DOC-002 parse defect.

## CORE-SD-X006 — Separate published channel state from a/c host-auth phase and command authority

**Observed:** SD publishes inherited auth after Core returns SCP wrapper. For a/c, inspected SCP11 draft §4.3 describes host authentication using submitted chain and first correct-MAC APDU after establishment. SD exposes no applet-authority flag/preflight. b test asserts general ApduException from Generate-then-Delete, without exact status or proving which command failed. c test lists key metadata already available without host auth, so it checks protected communication, not restricted administration. Core admission permits broader parameter shapes than fixed P-256/AES128 profile; SD adds no general validation. Aliases SD-DEP-001/002, SD-IMP-003/007 and B6-C009/C010/C013 remain.

**Documentation:** retain existing b/host distinction and explicit draft qualifications in interface `25–31,249–256`, README `30–37,139–163`; add first-post-setup-command phase beside a/c explanation and identify flag as setup history rather than live device security level. Narrow c test comment `67` “authenticated operation” to protected key listing. Keep generated-key comment already corrected at Scp11Tests `24–25,70`. **Runtime/decision:** no new auth property, privileged probe or validation restriction authorized. Resolve target final GP/YubiKey profile before stronger permission/counter assertions. **Qualification:** final 1.4 and exact vendor clauses unavailable after bounded research; no draft or sibling agreement promoted to final compliance.

**Reopen when:** setup completion/auth flag/profile admission, trust provisioning or first protected APDU changes. SD role/task XML/guides, Core SCP11 summary/parameter comments, integration auth/allowlist descriptions and migration actor distinction require review together. ## CORE-SD-X007 — Qualify actual empty-query, Le and chaining journeys

**Observed:** SD GET DATA defaults to no payload and Le 0; ListKeyInformation, card recognition and CA retrieval routinely take that path. Under SCP03 Core pads/encrypts empty command contrary to inspected final 1.1.2 §6.2.6. Pinned Python also pads; that agreement does not close B6-C011. Extended/short formatters always append Le; short accepts 0..255, not explicit 256. Large certificate requests/STORE can chain. Protected response/error/61xx treatment needs B6-C012 independent wire oracle. The INS 82 exemption is not reached by normal post-setup SD methods; raw reset 82 bypasses it entirely.

**Documentation:** clarify default zero and actual encoding near interface GET DATA `40–46`, with nearby configured-format bounds; describe STORE DATA `287` as one logical command with Core fragmentation. Preserve real exact-wire unit assertions unchanged, without presenting them as ISO/final GP conformance. **Runtime:** all protocol mechanisms remain B6, not new SD accepted defects. **Decision:** exact supported edition/profile and empty/Le/chaining behavior must be settled there; SD consumes the outcome. **Qualification:** no device tamper, response-chain, empty-wire or error-oracle execution. Draft 1.1.2.6 clauses remain uninspected, and ISO target clauses remain unavailable.

**Reopen when:** B6 formatting/encryption/chaining/status behavior changes. SD GET/STORE XML, factory options, test exact byte descriptions, certificate flow, README secure-task guidance and SHARED raw-tier examples must be checked together. Backend remains unchanged: it accurately forwards the selected graph and adds no independent wire policy.

## CORE-SD-X008 — Keep test coverage and resource claims at their actual oracle

**Observed:** full tests/helpers were read, including cleanup. Several configuration factory tests assert nonnull only; convenience “DisposesSession” asserts transmission, not disposal (comment already precise). Fixture CMAC KAT checks four RFC values, not host cryptogram/MAC, empty commands or full reset interoperability. Fake Dispose clears only StaticKeys; derived arrays/wire captures remain. Secure reset test does not scope-dispose its borrowed fake. Integration classes use static 100-second CTS, some calls omit tokens, many inline Defaults/Scp11 parameters and loaded certificates/providers are undisposed. a/c PKCS12 helpers export D then clone it into ECPrivateKey without clearing exported array; omitted root certificates stay separately owned. Same test token in local cleanup may already be canceled; Track base adds independent 60-second cleanup only for tracked tests. These are SD-IMP-007/008 refinements, not comment-only fixes.

**Documentation:** retain accurate existing oracle qualifications; correct c “authenticated operation” and lifecycle cleanup comments that promise restored defaults rather than request them. Test README says hardware required correctly but could state fixture/request/cleanup scope together. **Runtime:** strengthen harness, cleanup and exact failure/status/positive-control assertions in a separately authorized test task. **Decision:** choose intended security oracle before adding assertions; no renamed test or new assertion here. **Qualification:** tests have not run. Certificate bundle tests create native-backed certs if executed, and compilation alone is not that evidence.

**Reopen when:** fixture verification/disposal, helper ownership, assertion status/positive control, tokens or test restore policy changes. Exact files in test-oracles.md and file ledger are candidate-associated unchanged with explicit reasons. Test doc fragments with owned parameters and independent cleanup are retained as good examples, still uncompiled in this assignment.

## CORE-OATH-X001 — Explain state and borrowed metadata across the session lifetime

**Documentation:** `IOathSession` inherits Core readiness/auth without a local explanation separating
SCP setup from OATH unlock. Salt XML at lines 31–33 omits its session-owned alias lifetime. `OathSession` lines 49–55
returns cached applet state without a disposal guard; disposing zeroes salt/challenge but leaves
IsLocked, IsPasswordProtected, DeviceId and FirmwareVersion values. Public task guidance should say that
these are session observations, while operations refuse a terminal session. Describe Salt as borrowed
until disposal and direct callers to fresh creation after RESET. Avoid promising all getters throw or
that retained IsAuthenticated proves channel health after a secure-wire recovery latch.

**Runtime:** no new implementation defect allocated. Flags and metadata behavior are source facts;
B5-C001 owns common state/query semantics. **Decision:** changing terminal getter policy would require
separate API/compatibility work. **Qualification:** reset/plain/SCP fake assertions cover inherited flags
and actual old Salt views, not every cached getter or live secure reset.

**Reopen:** `src/Oath/src/IOathSession.cs` type and DeviceId/Salt/IsLocked/IsPasswordProtected members;
`src/Oath/src/OathSession.cs` properties, ApplyInitialization and Dispose; `src/Oath/README.md`
Getting started, User interaction, Constraints and Migrating reset callers; `src/Oath/CLAUDE.md`
Module Context and Reset and timestamp boundaries. Keep `src/Core/src/Abstractions/IApplicationSession.cs`,
`src/Core/src/Sessions/ApplicationSession.cs`, Core README session/query sections and
`docs/migration/v1-to-v2.md` OATH password/reset sections with the SHARED editor. Trigger: acceptance of
this local clarification or any changed readiness/getter/recovery/reset semantics. Existing terminal
reset guidance is retained, not reopened as a missing implementation.

## CORE-OATH-X002 — Scope workflow disposal to actual OATH calls

**Documentation:** OATH consumers need the actionable rule to await complete public workflows before
disposal and to keep callback/prompt resources alive. Core's guard protects one exchange, while
CalculateAll custom-period followups, AuthenticateAndRetry's provider/Validate/retry and calculation
callbacks extend beyond it. The README's cancellation paragraph correctly discusses an admitted exchange;
retain that precision and add the whole-task lifetime nearby rather than imply an operation-wide lock.

**Runtime:** secondary application of **CORE-B5-C006**, with B1 admission/drain/release distinction.
No duplicate lifetime bug allocation. Concurrent disposal may make followup fail or race post-exchange
state updates; callback-created detached work lies outside the awaited callback. **Decision:** a future
workflow lease/reentrancy policy belongs to Core and affected applets. **Qualification:** current OATH
reset held-LIST test checks overlap refusal and finally drain; it does not hold a post-wire callback or
an aggregate gap. Source race analysis is not an executed schedule or hardware failure.

**Reopen:** IOathSession type, CalculateAsync/CalculateCodeAsync/CalculateAllAsync and both retry overloads;
OathSession notification/aggregate/retry/dispose comments; README User interaction/Constraints/password
tasks; CLAUDE User-presence notifications; OathTool SessionHelper, AccessCommand and AccountsCommand
enclosing ownership. SHARED handoff: ApplicationSession/ExchangeGuard XML, Core README/CLAUDE concurrency,
`docs/usage/user-interaction.md`, `docs/architecture/raw-access-tiers.md` and migration session ownership.
Trigger: accepted clarification or actual workflow-admission/disposal change. Preserve borrowed
connection ownership and await real tasks before clearing inputs/results even if an outer wait ends.

## CORE-OATH-X003 — Qualify the secure terminal-reset oracle and actual SCP callers

**Documentation:** `OathScpResetTests.cs:76–77` says no encrypted-payload emulator is needed; explain why
that is a deliberate synthetic cleanup oracle, with no outbound encryption/MAC verification. The linked
csproj comment 27 identifies RFC 4493-validated primitive reuse; retain primitive versus whole-SCP scope.
The test observes actual Core key arrays, disposal state, command headers/order and borrowed connection
count. It is valuable even while wire/profile qualification remains outstanding.

**Runtime:** secondary handoff to **CORE-B6-C011/C012** for empty LIST/RESET/A5 commands and status/chaining;
**C002/C005/C006/C007/C009/C010** for response copies, phase, initializer cleanup and parameter/profile
questions. No duplicate wire ID or reopening of source-resolved IMP-010. **Decision:** final edition and
YubiKey profile targets must be settled by B6/coordinator, without silently treating code-cited 1.1.2.6
Public Review as final 1.1.2. **Qualification:** no live SCP terminal-reset proof. Serial 125's `6A88` prevented
the ceremony; no additional native/device/crypto execution occurred here.

**Reopen:** `src/Oath/tests/Yubico.YubiKit.Oath.UnitTests/OathScpResetTests.cs` complete test/fake/CMAC
assertions and UnitTests csproj lines 27–28; IntegrationTests `OathLifecycleTimeTests.ResetWithScp03_DefaultKeys_EndsSessionAndRequiresExplicitReopen`;
IOathSession ResetAsync/CreateAsync options XML; OathSession InitializeAsync/ResetAsync; README secure-channel
requirements/reset migration; CLAUDE Firmware Requirements/Reset boundaries; nested tests instructions;
TestExtensions/OathTestStateExtensions full reset/body/exception scopes. SHARED: Core SCP/response/key XML,
Core README SCP and response ownership, raw tiers, TLV/user-interaction guides, migration SCP/OATH reset.
Trigger: wire fix, changed standards/profile target, or new exact device lane. Keep first-successful-RESET
terminal behavior distinct from inability to reach that success on hardware.

## CORE-OATH-X005 — Keep test descriptions and cleanup claims assertion-accurate

**Documentation:** Unit `OathSessionTests.cs:115–186` labels DeriveKey tests, but these call BCL PBKDF2
directly; describe determinism/difference of that direct algorithm use, not session method coverage or an
independent known-answer vector. `CredentialDataTests.cs:610–617` calls an unpadded input StandardPadded
and asserts only nonempty. Keep comments at that oracle scope; stronger exact-byte vectors already live
in OathInputTests/Core Base32Tests. `OathSessionTests` factory-failure remarks at lines 628–632 should keep their
6A82 fake retry condition, rather than imply every failed factory leaves a device reusable. Generic
cleanup/reset prose in older integration helpers must not imply restoration after arbitrary failure.

**Runtime:** selected test-scaffolding debt, separate from the fourteen fixed product scopes: integration
NewToken helpers allocate undisposed CTS; password derivation helpers create untracked UTF-8 arrays;
AuditV2 raw PUT leaves seed/payload copies uncleared and raw DELETE ignores statuses with no verification;
PasswordChange finally can attempt new-password cleanup before rotation succeeded and replace the first
failure. Unit authentication fake owns retained snapshots/response arrays but several tests never dispose
the borrowed fake. These are not assertions of real-secret compromise or product regression.
**Decision:** separately scope harness cleanup/first-error policy; keep executable assertions unchanged
in this documentation pass. **Qualification:** no execution. A successful body return or disposal count

## CORE-OATH-X006 — Make selection and example resource prerequisites explicit

**Documentation:** IYubiKeyExtensions remarks at line 42 and README Constraints at line 230 describe one physical key's
one-live-connection headline without nearby process/known-member/disjoint-view conditions. Link and retain
the useful Core bound rather than promise global exclusivity. README Getting started's unfiltered
FindFirst can select a key without SmartCard; a task example can select by SupportsConnection or explicitly
choose SmartCard discovery, explaining different scope/census behavior. OathTool's selection really uses All
and first eligible in noninteractive mode; it is not an implementation of SmartCard-scoped discovery.

README reset migration at lines 252–259 uses undeclared `ct`, and shared migration's retry example at lines 706–745 leaves
callback-returned password ownership implicit. Classify them as composable fragments with explicit typed
prerequisites, or supply complete ownership including source/result cleanup and options/parameters live
through fresh creation. Do not copy the password provider as an expression that loses its buffer owner.

**Runtime:** secondary A/B1 selection/known-member limitation only; no new discovery bug. **Decision:**
choosing All/local filtering versus a scoped view is application policy; no change to default selection
authorized. **Qualification:** current selector tests substitute discovery/live metadata while retaining
real filtering/Spectre prompt. They prove cancellation/no OATH open after late metadata, not native census,
recovery of serial 9681620 or every host's console behavior. Examples remain VALID-NOT-CHECKED.

**Reopen:** IYubiKeyExtensions create/one-shot XML; README Getting started/Constraints/Migrating reset callers;
OathTool DeviceSelector/OathToolServices/Program descriptions and device-selection test comments. SHARED:
`docs/usage/device-discovery.md`, physical-device-model/discovery-guarantees, Core README selection/sharing,
`docs/migration/v1-to-v2.md` lines 463–578 and 706–745, map OATH/reset/password entries (DOC-002 parsing remains
its old identity). Trigger: accepted task/example correction or actual selection/ownership migration.
Package README remains a useful unchanged short entry point; no new broad API guarantees are needed there.

## X002 — Explain the facade's whole-ceremony lifetime

**Documentation:** extend W/src/Client/WebAuthnClient.cs:24–45 and README Constraints with fully awaited,
serialized ceremony ownership before disposal and prompt resources through actual late work. Existing
session-transfer and returned-buffer qualifications remain accurate. **Runtime:** client/backend bool
flags change after awaited disposal; backend disposes shared PIN protocol before awaiting session.

client operation join or concurrent-disposal gate. **Decision:** future workflow admission, shared
disposal and reentrancy design belongs to separately selected implementation work; do not invent a lease
API. **Qualification:** current substitute disposal-count tests establish one call in one sequential
scenario. Reopen Client/Backend/ceremony/extension lifetime XML, both module guides, user-interaction/raw
tiers, migration ownership guidance, Construction/CeremonyFrame/Backend/intent tests when this changes.
This carries B5-C006 / CTAP-X002 rather than counting another generic Core bug.

## X004 — Preserve the two prompt owners and outcome boundaries

**Documentation:** retain sessionOptions.UserPresencePrompt versus clientOptions.CredentialPrompt.
Clarify W UnitTests/Client/UserPresenceIntentTests.cs:30–32: its real CTAP/Core session and SmartCard

captures ambient intent in caller flow at notification creation; lower protocol requests; CTAP backend
resolves from status before typed decode. Generic ClientPin and GetNext are silent; a successful CTAP

uses None and can delay return after timeout. CTAP-X020's throwing-logger path can bypass backend
cleanup after callback failure. **Decision:** retain callback/diagnostic-failure resilience as distinct
selected work; no new WebAuthn progress/prompt policy. **Qualification:** intent tests inspect request
context only, not resolved outcomes/native waits/physical gestures. Reopen K notification/intent/XML,
C backend and session/presence XML, W interaction/CeremonyDeadline and intent-test commentary, both
guides and docs/usage/user-interaction.md after outcome/capture/callback-drain changes.

Aliases WA-IMP-006/013, CTAP-IMP-004/027 and CTAP-X004/X013/X014/X016/X019; B6-C002/C006 remain distinct.

builder/storage XML; K ApduResponse/FIDO/SCP buffer rationale; actual retained-buffer observers after
each selected repair. Public identifier metadata is not classified as secret merely because received.

source_definition.text:
## CORE-OTP-X001 — Keep creation and workflow ownership local

**Observed:** `IYubiKeyExtensions.cs:108–140` selects one transport, creates one hidden
connection and calls `OwnConnection` only after `YubiOtpSession.CreateAsync` succeeds.
Core's helper disposes a successfully opened connection if initialization fails.
The direct factory at `YubiOtpSession.cs:124–169` borrows the connection and binds
before reads. Backends borrow the effective protocol and retain no IDisposable state.
Core's platform owner controls native resources; the applet does not acquire a second
physical claim. Known member IDs coordinate process-local opens, with A/B1's partial
grouping/disjoint-view limits. Direct expert opens acquire no grouped-key registration.

`SmartCardBackend.WriteUpdateAsync:91–122` can make configuration and status calls in
two guard intervals. Sequence validation and `_status` publication occur after those
exchanges. HID response CRC/terminal resolution also occurs after Core releases its
exchange guard. ApplicationSession drains an admitted exchange, not the complete
public method, configuration object, callback task or provisioning workflow.

- **Documentation:** qualify README Constraints 324–329 and interface general remarks;
  retain complete session-before-connection scopes. Explain that callers await each
  complete operation and keep borrowed configurations/services alive through their use.
- **Runtime:** reuse B5 C006 and B1 ownership findings nonadditively. No new applet-wide
  lock or lifetime lease is authorized. The current backend shape needs no disposal hook.
- **Decision:** maintainers select any future whole-operation serialization/disposal policy.
- **Qualification:** Linux cross-layer borrowed reuse is a fake-native managed oracle;
  idle/sequential reuse and uncertain protocol recovery remain separate.
- **Reopen:** XML on factories/interface, README/CLAUDE, DeviceHelper and all complete
  task scopes; shared physical model, ownership guide, raw tiers and migration when
  connection claims, teardown or workflow admission changes. Keep unchanged accurate
  factory XML; it already distinguishes hidden and borrowed connections.

Aliases: `yubiotp-001:OTP-DEP-001`, `OTP-DEP-003`; B1 C005/C008, B5 C004/C006.

source_definition.text:
## CORE-OTP-X002 — Preserve HID initialization, polling and recovery classification

**Observed:** Core `OtpHidProtocol.cs:90–129,463–479` reads one report for protocol
firmware, performs the NEO refresh when that first major is three, then reads another
report for returned six-byte status. `HidBackend.cs:44–53` prefers that first protocol
version; `YubiOtpSession.cs:147–166` caches the second status and applies an override
only afterward. `Configure` then finds initialization already complete in this public
route. Its synchronous lazy wait remains reachable through other internal/raw paths.

Built-in Linux/macOS typed paths enforce eight-byte successful input; the Windows
compatibility adapter checks its returned report length. A caller-supplied
`IOtpHidConnection` reaches Core's indexing/slicing without a central length check.
Malformed custom input can therefore produce indexing/slicing exceptions before the
applet's six-byte write check. The interface contract says eight bytes; defensive
malformed-response behavior still needs a deliberate policy and meaningful test.

The NEO invalid-map probe catches every failure while `_resetFailure` remains null,
including readiness/transport failures after a successful abort. Python catches only
CommandRejectedError. This broad catch and tight three-second readiness loop are B5
C007 mechanisms, now traced into actual YubiOTP initialization. They are not new
independent applet bugs or a claim that the invalid map changed persistent settings.

- **Documentation:** add two-report/effective-version provenance and local timing
  conditions to initialization guidance. Describe 1 s write-ready polling with 5 ms
  busy delay, 3 s readiness with no explicit busy delay, 250 ms touch polling with
  the local 14 s threshold, and bounded packet count separately from native duration.
- **Runtime:** refer report-size admission, NEO catch and polling cadence to B5 C007;
  tests should use the public applet path, including malformed first and second reads.
- **Decision:** choose custom-provider malformed exception policy and classified NEO
  rejection behavior without copying Python's timing/ownership policy wholesale.
- **Qualification:** elapsed checks run between awaited native calls; a held GET/SET
  can exceed them. Only `OtpHidTouchTimeoutException` becomes TimedOut. NEO timeout
  swallowed during initialization emits no presence outcome because the probe uses None.
- **Reopen:** `HidBackend.ReadInitialStateAsync`, session initialization, CLAUDE/README,
  Core OTP comments, raw tiers, creation/recovery and Linux cross-layer test commentary
  after report admission, version source, NEO catch, polling or reset policy changes.

Aliases: `yubiotp-001:OTP-DEP-002/004`, `OTP-IMP-005/006`; B5 C001/C007/C008.

source_definition.text:
## CORE-OTP-X003 — Trace every secret-derived response owner

**Observed:** HID data responses travel from successful native GET arrays into Core's
cleared pooled accumulator, then an independent assembled array, then an applet prefix
view. Core clears payload/frame/output report and accumulator, while successful incoming
report arrays remain intact (`OtpHidProtocol.cs:327–390,484–489`). Linux and macOS
owners explicitly transfer those arrays. Windows adds another report-ID buffer on
GET and SET (`WindowsHidReportAccess.cs:111–148`) that is not cleared by the adapter's
outer copy cleanup. These are B5 C005/B4 C007, with actual HMAC/AES callers identified.

SmartCard serial/HMAC/AES calls pass through the APDU pipeline; `ApduResponse` clones
raw transport response. `SmartCardBackend.cs:153–166` returns a prefix alias of its
Data, not the response owner. Clearing the returned segment reaches that prefix,
leaving excess data/status and the transport source copy distinct. Failure cleanup
clears the whole Data view under ordinary callback/logging behavior. B6 owns raw,
fragment, decrypted/SCP and response-carrier cleanup; keep those shared mechanisms
under B6 C002 rather than allocating another applet defect for each copy.

`UserPresenceNotification.ResolveAsync` logs a callback failure when a primary failure
exists. A throwing logging provider can itself escape before each backend's subsequent
zeroing statement. This conditional all-path limit belongs with C C008/B5 C005, not a
claim that ordinary prompt-failure zeroing is absent. Existing backend tests do observe
their actual response arrays becoming zero on ordinary terminal callback failures.

- **Documentation:** retain caller source/result cleanup and avoid all-copy assurances.
  Clarify the result view versus complete owned response and lower staging scopes.
- **Runtime:** reuse shared copy/logging groups; define receive ownership before adding
  clearing to custom-provider results that may be borrowed or reused.
- **Decision:** select transfer/copy/clearable-owner contracts and cleanup precedence;
  do not apply MemoryMarshal writable conversion to arbitrary borrowed memory.
- **Qualification:** only semantically sensitive HMAC/AES/challenge/configuration data
  requires secret cleanup. Serial/status/firmware metadata alone needs no secret zeroing.
- **Reopen:** both backends, calculation XML, README security/result examples, Core raw
  tiers/APDU response docs, platform report comments, terminal-callback and retained-array
  tests after any owner/transfer/clear/logging behavior change. Existing accurate
  configuration-source and callback-before-transfer prose remains unchanged context.

## CORE-OTP-X004 — Retain a one-shot result until hidden-session teardown succeeds

**Observed:** `IYubiKeyExtensions.CalculateHmacSha1Async:83–94` evaluates a successful
calculation result inside `await using`, then awaits session disposal before its own
task can transfer that result. If protocol/owned-connection disposal throws, the helper
faults and gives the caller no result view to clear. The backend already considers
its output transferred. This is a distinct outer producer boundary, extending
`yubiotp-001:OTP-IMP-003`; ordinary successful disposal is unaffected. No native failure
was induced and no result was recovered experimentally.

- **Documentation:** qualify one-shot result ownership on exceptional teardown; keep
  source/input cleanup in caller finally even when session creation/disposal fails.
- **Runtime:** propose explicit result retention and failure clearing in later scoped
  work; avoid changing the public response type during this documentation investigation.
- **Decision:** maintainers choose primary-operation versus teardown exception policy
  and whether successful output may ever transfer alongside a teardown diagnostic.
- **Qualification:** use a deterministic fake connection with valid synthetic CRC and
  throwing/held DisposeAsync. Distinguish backend success, zeroing and outer task outcome.
- **Reopen:** the extension's XML/body, one-shot README example 164–185, interface output
  ownership, backend transfer explanation and extension lifecycle tests after a fix.
  GetConfigState/Put one-shots remain context because they return no sensitive calculation
  buffer; preserve their current resource scopes rather than labeling them defective.

## CORE-OTP-X005 — Keep configuration and parser lifetimes outside exchange drain

**Observed:** `SlotConfiguration.GetConfig:150–184` copies secrets before validating
new-code length; `YubiOtpSession.WriteConfigAsync:529–549` obtains config bytes and
validates/appends current code before its finally. These retained OTP-IMP-003 paths
remain unchanged. Normal source/config/assembled-frame clearing reaches separate owners.
The session copies config synchronously at call start, while config disposal is still
the caller's responsibility. A guard around one exchange does not own it.

Standalone ChalResp/Hotp/Static commands acquire secrets before parsing access-code
text and before cleanup try. The unified `OtpStaticCommand` correctly translates text
but builds its disposable config before parsing access code and entering try
(`OtpCommands.cs:531–571`); a parse failure can strand that config. This narrow CLI
handoff preserves OTP-IMP-003/010 and the correct historical N3 encoding fix.

- **Documentation:** retain existing preflight qualifications, separate mutable source,
  immutable string, config fields, GetConfig array and transport staging lifetimes.
- **Runtime:** later engineering should validate before secret acquisition or guard every
  acquired owner immediately. Do not repair sample runtime under Pass 1.
- **Decision:** define exceptional-path cleanup/diagnostic policy with the actual CLI owner.
- **Qualification:** actual-array observers and parse-failure/no-I/O vectors are meaningful;
  post-disposal refusal and no-I/O alone do not prove erasure.
- **Reopen:** base/config/session XML, sample setter comments, unified CLI static command,
  security task examples and migration ownership after validation/cleanup changes.

source_definition.text:
## CORE-OTP-X006 — Separate firmware policy, capability and presence certainty

**Observed:** SmartCard initialization probes Management on both USB/NFC, uses it when
parseable, and takes the greater version when raw OTP major is three. HID uses first
protocol report firmware. Override governs effective session gates and SmartCard
sequence-bypass interval, while cached ConfigState gates and SmartCard touch heuristic
use raw status. Major-zero policy admits features and configuration types; it is no
proof of actual firmware generation or operation support.

HID backend resolves after length/CRC; SmartCard resolves after APDU success/minimum
length. SmartCard PolicyRequires comes from keyboard-trigger cached bits, not read-back
of RequireTouch. A successful calculation after post-admission cancellation can resolve
Completed. A callback-induced pre-admission cancellation test is a different oracle.

- **Documentation:** preserve local source/override/transport conditions. Avoid deriving
  OTP support from Core algorithm catalog applicability, general SCP floors or FIPS bits.
- **Runtime:** retain OTP-IMP-004/005/006/012 and B5/C policy owners; no heuristic repair
  or support expansion is authorized. SmartCard status prefix/sequence gaps stay applet-owned.
- **Decision:** choose supported command/interface/version matrix and prompt certainty.
- **Qualification:** old serial 103 results include raw/effective 0.0.1, metadata
  5.8.0.beta.0, USB CCID HMAC rejection 6985 and successful HID calculations. Retain those
  facts without universalizing CCID rejection, major-zero support, NFC or old firmware.
- **Reopen:** firmware/ConfigState/session/configuration XML, both backends, requirement
  tables, shared interaction, migration and prompt/firmware tests after provenance,
  override, capability or certainty changes. Preserve existing HMAC marker/AES verifier
  qualifications and their original finding scopes.

## CORE-OTP-X007 — Route keyboard and credential responsibilities to actual callers

**Observed:** `StaticPasswordSlotConfiguration.cs:148–177` uses Core translator indexers
after a full validation pass; it avoids the generic GetHidCodes string→char-array helper.
Standalone OtpTool StaticCommand still sends UTF-8 bytes as scan codes and ignores
layout. Unified `OtpHelpers.CreateStaticPasswordConfiguration` uses the working string
overload. Its generator includes both cases from ModHex's supported map, yielding
32 non-whitespace letters, rather than its comment's 16-letter description.

Neither static caller uses ConsoleCredentialReader. That reader's redirected line
confirmation fix is a separate historical N3 scope. Its encoded credential bytes are
not HID translation. Correcting Core reader documentation cannot fix the standalone
sample; changing the sample cannot prove a locale table renders on every host.

- **Documentation:** qualify README's “layout-independent/neutral” wording to supported
  host layouts and selected characters; retain B4 C010's mapping/alias/locale limits.
- **Runtime:** keep OTP-IMP-009 under the standalone applet sample; refer generator prose
  to B4 C010 and early unified-CLI config lifetime to X005.
- **Decision:** select supported keyboard layouts/characters and production credential
  input policy; keep immutable CLI strings and printed secrets visible in that decision.
- **Qualification:** current literal en_US lowercase/uppercase and ModHex byte vectors
  prove encoding. Physical keyboard output, dead keys/host state and older capacities
  require a later coordinated editor/input-capture lane, never a shell or unattended touch.
- **Reopen:** static constructor/XML and README static example, Core translator docs,
  standalone layout/help comments, unified helper prose/tests and migration static row
  after mapping or caller routing changes. Preserve working string helper and exact
  literal vectors; do not imply all CLI paths share the broken standalone implementation.

Aliases: `audit-v2-20261022-20261031:N3`, `yubiotp-001:OTP-IMP-009/010`; B4 C010, C C001–C004.

source_definition.text:
## CORE-OTP-X008 — Resolve the migration relocation question by named surface

**Observed:** complete YubiOtp API and Management interface/DeviceConfig review finds
no typed QueryFipsMode, SetLegacyDeviceConfig or SetMode API. A complete current
public-snapshot name search corroborates those absences. Management **does** expose
GetDeviceInfoAsync, delegated to Core DeviceInfoReader. Its OTP path sends capabilities
command 0x13, validates the declared prefix/CRC and supports pages. Modern
SetDeviceConfigAsync serializes Management TLVs, with effective 5.0.0 write gate;
it is not the old four-byte mode/timeout/eject command. Raw session command access
remains an expert escape hatch rather than a relocated typed implementation.

- **Documentation:** update only active YubiOTP migration entries 246–254 and the
  outstanding-verification row 419 to split device-info relocation, absent typed
  FIPS-mode query and absent legacy mutator. Keep point-in-time historical surveys intact.
- **Runtime:** no new missing Core feature is allocated. Core FipsCapable/FipsApproved
  mapping concerns remain A C004; these metadata fields are not an OTP FIPS-mode query.
- **Decision:** maintainers select whether legacy query/mutation deserves a typed v2 API.
- **Qualification:** this is a source-surface inventory at the pin, not old-key device
  compatibility, equivalence of every v1 response or successful modern/legacy execution.
- **Reopen:** migration map/gaps/guide and YubiOtp/Management public reference if named
  APIs arrive, disappear or change gates. Retain README Related Management link, which
  already routes device-level enabling correctly. Library generation conveniences,
  TOTP, NDEF read-back and 38/45 scan-map findings keep their exact applet scopes.

Alias: `yubiotp-001:OTP-DEP-005`; Management boundary owns complete read/write enforcement.

## CORE-OTP-X009 — Keep actual assertion and qualification scopes

**Observed:** all assigned tests and helpers were read. Linux cross-layer tests exercise
actual production slot/device/native owner over fake report seams. Backend callback
tests inspect actual returned arrays; same-helper CRC generation is not an independent
known answer. Twelve HMAC device vectors have historical one-key execution, separate
from this packet's zero executions. The misleading high-byte/length/dispose test names
already have appropriately narrow comments and need no churn.

Held Linux creation releases its first-GET gate in finally but obtains/disposes its
first session only on the success path; an intervening assertion can skip disposal.
Protection cleanup calls are sequential, so first deletion failure skips slot one.
Programming often occurs before a cleanup try. These extend OTP-IMP-011 and B5 C008,
with no test assertion or helper changes here.

- **Documentation:** retain source/assertion versus executed-evidence language and
  per-device/firmware/transport limits. Correct the small stale CRC “no flags” comment
  at SlotConfigurationTests 1043–1049 if that unit is edited: defaults remain present.
- **Runtime:** strengthen meaningful failure-path release/drain and independent CRC,
  exact interval/zero rules, custom-report and one-shot output oracles separately.
- **Decision:** select each test's intended contract before changing assertions that
  deliberately pin erroneous current IMF behavior or permissive sequence rules.
- **Qualification:** preserve NFC read-back, old firmware, keyboard output, Windows
  late-handoff and PIV physical deferrals. No new build/test/hardware execution occurred.
- **Reopen:** named test units, nested instructions and module test/qualification guides
  after fixtures/assertions/cleanup change; remove later edited overlaps from clean sampling.

## CORE-HSM-X001 — Explain reset, readiness and channel history locally

**Observed:** `HsmAuthSession.ResetAsync:507–519` preserves its backend, version and public ready/auth
flags, sends protected RESET when SCP is active, then performs an unprotected re-SELECT through the same
secure graph. It retains no SCP parameters and starts no fresh handshake. Its comment claims that a
PC/SC transaction remains owned, although this protocol path creates none. `IsAuthenticated` is inherited
Core channel-setup history, unchanged by management/credential operations, recovery latch or re-SELECT.

**Documentation:** propose a concise local auth distinction and reset failure/secure-channel qualification
in `src/YubiHsm/src/IHsmAuthSession.cs` type and Reset remarks, `HsmAuthSession.cs` initializer/reset comment,
`README.md` Constraints/Requirements and `CLAUDE.md` Module Context/version/reset explanation. Keep the
existing version-retention statement. Remove the unsupported transaction rationale in a fresh prose edit.
`IYubiKeyExtensions.cs` connection ownership remains useful and needs consistency review, not a rewrite.

**Runtime/decision:** decide HSM reset's desired terminal/reinitialize policy, full-workflow admission and
auth-state meaning separately. This report does not select OATH's different terminal-reset behavior or
claim measured device breakage. Aliases: B5-C001/C006; B6-C011/C012/C015; `HSM-DEP-001/002`.

**Qualification:** an independently traced fake and an authorized identified SCP-capable YubiKey must
separate RESET success, SELECT result, retained/retired host state, next protected operation, teardown and
fresh handshake. Existing override-only reset test establishes none of these secure steps. Preserve
serial 125's two 6A88 setup failures before EXTERNAL AUTHENTICATE/RESET.

**Reopen:** channel/reset implementation or policy changes → the XML/guides above,
`tests/...UnitTests/HsmAuthSessionByteLevelTests.cs` reset commentary,
`tests/...IntegrationTests/TestExtensions/HsmAuthTestStateExtensions.cs`, `src/YubiHsm/tests/CLAUDE.md`,
tool `ResetCommand.cs`, `ResetMenu.cs`, `HsmAuthExamples/ResetHsmAuth.cs`; shared Core session/raw-tier
guidance and `docs/migration/v1-to-v2.md`, `v1-to-v2-map.yml`, `v1-to-v2-gaps.md`,
`docs/v1-to-v2-comparison.md`, `docs/v2-highlights.md` HSM/reset/SCP entries. Shared editor owns those
files. Migration YAML DOC-002 remains separate.

## CORE-HSM-X002 — State reachable buffer cleanup, with explicit response ownership

**Observed:** successful CALCULATE owns a final response, copies three keys, resolves success, and clears
that response even when Parse or success-resolution fails. The current write-through helper reaches
the real array; the sealed Core response now offers `Clear()`. Raw transport results, fragments, failed
writer staging and SCP decrypted temporary copies remain independent. Retry/backend errors can throw
before the successful-response clearing scope. Error data must be classified by actual semantics rather
than presumed secret or harmless. TLVs are disposed after entry into the encoder; caller input remains
borrowed and inline construction failure has a narrower cleanup scope.

**Documentation:** retain the already precise owned-copy language, add the lower-layer scope only where
an end-to-end guarantee might otherwise be inferred. Route owner API commentary through Core's explicit
`ApduResponse.Clear` contract. Scope standalone Parse/source/additional-copy responsibilities precisely.
Affected: `HsmAuthSession.cs` calculate/ZeroApduResponse internal rationale, `SessionKeys.cs` XML,
module README Security notes and CLAUDE buffer handling; `SessionKeysTests.cs` helper/zeroing assertions.

**Runtime/decision:** a future implementation can replace the legacy helper with the explicit owner API
and address actual remaining copies/exceptional allocations with identity-based cleanup oracles. No
write-through consumer sample or blanket "zero everything returned by a key" policy is proposed.
Aliases: `HSM-DEP-003`, `HSM-IMP-002`; C-C005–C007/C020; B6-C002/C006/C007. Current local helper is
source-functional, so this is not a new demonstrated failure to clear its response.

**Qualification/reopen:** changed owner/encoder/formatter/transport/secure-response cleanup → all those
surfaces, `src/Core/src/Utilities/Tlv*.cs`, APDU response/transmitter/chaining/SCP XML, Core README/CLAUDE,
`docs/usage/tlv-processing.md`, raw-access tiers, migration ownership entries and samples that copy keys.
Existing SessionKeys disposal test captures all three actual arrays; ZeroApduResponse test observes final
raw owner only. Neither asserts transport/decrypt/fragment cleanup or failed allocation cleanup.
source_definition.heading: CORE-HSM-X002 — State reachable buffer cleanup, with explicit response ownership
